2.11.m: Making [the offering] in vessels of phalgu, one would attain all desires; / supreme brilliance and especially renown [is gained] in an arka vessel.

2.11.s:
bailve lakṣmīntathā medhāṃ nityamāyustathaiva ca /
kṣetrārāmataḍāgeṣu sarvasasyeṣu caiva ha //
2.11.d:
बैल्वे लक्ष्मीन्तथा मेधां नित्यमायुस्तथैव च ।
क्षेत्रारामतडागेषु सर्वसस्येषु चैव ह ॥
2.11.m: In a bilva vessel, [one gains] fortune, wisdom, and everlasting life; / and upon the fields, gardens, ponds, and all crops,

2.11.s:
varṣatya jasraṃ parjanyo veṇupātreṣu kurvataḥ /
eteṣveva supātreṣu bhojanāgramaśeṣataḥ //
2.11.d:
वर्षत्य जस्रं पर्जन्यो वेणुपात्रेषु कुर्वतः ।
एतेष्वेव सुपात्रेषु भोजनाग्रमशेषतः ॥
2.11.m: Parjanya rains incessantly for one who makes [offerings] in bamboo vessels. / In these very worthy vessels, one should always offer

2.11.s:
sadā dadyātsa yajñānāṃ sarveṣāṃ phalamāpnuyāt /
pitṛbhyaḥ puṣpamālyāni sugandhāni ca tatparaḥ //
2.11.d:
सदा दद्यात्स यज्ञानां सर्वेषां फलमाप्नुयात् ।
पितृभ्यः पुष्पमाल्यानि सुगन्धानि च तत्परः ॥
2.11.m: the first portion of food completely; he attains the fruit of all sacrifices. / Devoted to the Pitṛs, [offering] flowers, garlands, and fragrant perfumes to them,

2.11.s:
sadā dadyātkriyāyuktaḥ śa vibhāti divākaraḥ /
guggulādīṃstathā dhūpānpitṛbhyo yaḥ prayacchati //
2.11.d:
सदा दद्यात्क्रियायुक्तः श विभाति दिवाकरः ।
गुग्गुलादींस्तथा धूपान्पितृभ्यो यः प्रयच्छति ॥
2.11.m: he who always gives, engaged in the rite, shines like the sun. / He who presents incense such as guggulu to the Pitṛs,

2.11.s:
saṃyuktānmadhusarpirbhyaṃ so 'gniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet /
dhūpaṃ gandhaguṇopetaṃ kṛtvā pitṛparāyaṇaḥ //
2.11.d:
संयुक्तान्मधुसर्पिर्भ्यं सो ऽग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् ।
धूपं गन्धगुणोपेतं कृत्वा पितृपरायणः ॥
2.11.m: mixed with honey and clarified butter, obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice. / Having offered incense endowed with good fragrance, devoted to the Pitṛs,

2.11.s:
labhate ca suśarmāṇi iha cāmutra cobhayoḥ /
dadyādevaṃ pitṛbhyāstu nityameva hyatandritaḥ //
2.11.d:
लभते च सुशर्माणि इह चामुत्र चोभयोः ।
दद्यादेवं पितृभ्यास्तु नित्यमेव ह्यतन्द्रितः ॥
2.11.m: he attains great comfort in both worlds, here and hereafter. / Thus one should give to the Pitṛs continually and unwearied.

2.11.s:
dīpaṃ pitṛbhyaḥ prayataḥ sadā yastu prayacchati /
gatiṃ cāpratimaṃ cakṣustasmātsalabhate śubham //
2.11.d:
दीपं पितृभ्यः प्रयतः सदा यस्तु प्रयच्छति ।
गतिं चाप्रतिमं चक्षुस्तस्मात्सलभते शुभम् ॥
2.11.m: He who, restrained, always presents a lamp to the Pitṛs, / attains from that a high destination and peerless, auspicious sight.

2.11.s:
tejasā yaśasā caiva kāntyā cāpi balena ca /
bhuvi prakāśo bhavati brājate ca triviṣṭape //
2.11.d:
तेजसा यशसा चैव कान्त्या चापि बलेन च ।
भुवि प्रकाशो भवति ब्राजते च त्रिविष्टपे ॥
2.11.m: Through splendor, fame, beauty, and strength, / he becomes radiant on earth and shines in heaven.

2.11.s:
apsarobhiḥ parivṛto vimānāgre ca modate /
gandhapuṣpaiśca dhūpaiśva japāhutibhireva ca //
2.11.d:
अप्सरोभिः परिवृतो विमानाग्रे च मोदते ।
गन्धपुष्पैश्च धूपैश्व जपाहुतिभिरेव च ॥
2.11.m: Surrounded by Apsarases, he rejoices at the forefront of a heavenly chariot. / With perfumes, flowers, incenses, prayers, and oblations,

2.11.s:
phalamūlanamaskāraiḥ pitṝṇāṃ prayataḥ śuciḥ /
pūjāṃ kṛtvā dvijānpaścātpūjayedannasaṃpadā //
2.11.d:
फलमूलनमस्कारैः पितॄणां प्रयतः शुचिः ।
पूजां कृत्वा द्विजान्पश्चात्पूजयेदन्नसंपदा ॥
2.11.m: with fruits, roots, and obeisances, self-restrained and pure, / having offered worship to the ancestors, he should afterwards honor the twice-born with an abundance of food.

2.11.s:
śrāddhakāleṣu niyataṃ vāyubhūtāḥ pitāmahāḥ /
āviśanti dvijāñchreṣṭhāṃstasmādetadbravīmi te //
2.11.d:
श्राद्धकालेषु नियतं वायुभूताः पितामहाः ।
आविशन्ति द्विजाञ्छ्रेष्ठांस्तस्मादेतद्ब्रवीमि ते ॥
2.11.m: At the times of a śrāddha, having assumed the form of wind, the ancestors / regularly enter the best among the twice-born; therefore I declare this to you.

2.11.s:
vastrai ratnapradānaiśca bhakṣyaiḥ peyaistathaiva ca /
gobhiraśvaistathā grāmaiḥ pūjayeddvijasattamān //
2.11.d:
वस्त्रै रत्नप्रदानैश्च भक्ष्यैः पेयैस्तथैव च ।
गोभिरश्वैस्तथा ग्रामैः पूजयेद्द्विजसत्तमान् ॥
2.11.m: With garments, gifts of jewels, edible foods, and drinks likewise, / with cattle, horses, and villages, one should honor the best of the twice-born.

2.11.s:
bhavanti pitaraḥ prītāḥ pūjiteṣu dvijātiṣu /
tasmādyatnena vidhivatpūjayeta dvijānsadā //
2.11.d:
भवन्ति पितरः प्रीताः पूजितेषु द्विजातिषु ।
तस्माद्यत्नेन विधिवत्पूजयेत द्विजान्सदा ॥
2.11.m: The ancestors become pleased when the twice-born are honored; / therefore, one should always honor the twice-born according to the rules with diligence.

2.11.s:
savyottarābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ kuryādullekhanaṃ dvijāḥ /
prokṣaṇaṃ ca tataḥ kuryācchrāddhakarmaṇyatandritaḥ //
2.11.d:
सव्योत्तराभ्यां पाणिभ्यां कुर्यादुल्लेखनं द्विजाः ।
प्रोक्षणं च ततः कुर्याच्छ्राद्धकर्मण्यतन्द्रितः ॥
2.11.m: With both hands, the left placed above, the twice-born should make the furrow; / then, unwearied, he should perform the sprinkling in the rite of the śrāddha.

2.11.s:
darbhānpiṇḍāṃstathā bhakṣyānpuṣpāṇi vividhāni ca /
gandhadānamalaṅkāramekaikaṃ nirvaped budhaḥ //
2.11.d:
दर्भान्पिण्डांस्तथा भक्ष्यान्पुष्पाणि विविधानि च ।
गन्धदानमलङ्कारमेकैकं निर्वपेद् बुधः ॥
2.11.m: Darbha grass, balls of rice, edible foods, and various flowers, / the gift of perfume, and decoration—the wise man should offer each one separately.

2.11.s:
peṣayitvāñjanaṃ samyagviśveṣāmuttarottaram /
abhyaṅgaṃ darbhaviñjūlaistribhiḥ kuryādyathāvidhi //
2.11.d:
पेषयित्वाञ्जनं सम्यग्विश्वेषामुत्तरोत्तरम् ।
अभ्यङ्गं दर्भविञ्जूलैस्त्रिभिः कुर्याद्यथाविधि ॥
2.11.m: Having thoroughly ground collyrium, [offering it] one by one to all, / he should duly perform the anointing with three bundles of darbha grass.

2.11.s:
apasavyaṃ vitṛbhayaśca dadyādañjanamuttamam /
nipātya jānu sarveṣāṃ vastrārthaṃ sūtrameva vā //
2.11.d:
अपसव्यं वितृभयश्च दद्यादञ्जनमुत्तमम् ।
निपात्य जानु सर्वेषां वस्त्रार्थं सूत्रमेव वा ॥
2.11.m: With the sacred thread over the right shoulder, he should offer excellent collyrium to the ancestors, / having bent his knee, or thread for the sake of clothing to all of them.

2.11.s:
khaṇḍanaṃ prokṣaṇaṃ caiva tathaivollekhanaṃ dvijaḥ /
sakṛddevapitṝṇāṃ syātpitṝṇāṃ tribhirucyate //
2.11.d:
खण्डनं प्रोक्षणं चैव तथैवोल्लेखनं द्विजः ।
सकृद्देवपितॄणां स्यात्पितॄणां त्रिभिरुच्यते ॥
2.11.m: The scattering, the sprinkling, and likewise the furrowing, O twice-born, / should be done once for the gods and ancestors, but three times for the ancestors, it is said.

2.11.s:
ekaṃ pavitraṃ hastena pitṝnasarvānsakṛtsakṛt /
cailamantreṇa piṇḍebhyo dattvādarśāñjine hi tam //
2.11.d:
एकं पवित्रं हस्तेन पितॄनसर्वान्सकृत्सकृत् ।
चैलमन्त्रेण पिण्डेभ्यो दत्त्वादर्शाञ्जिने हि तम् ॥
2.11.m: Holding one purifier with the hand, [offering] once to each of all the ancestors, / having given it to the rice-balls with the garment-mantra, [he offers] collyrium on mirror-like surfaces.

2.11.s:
sadā sarpistilairyuktāṃstrīnpiṇḍānnirvapedbhuvi /
jānu kṛtvā tathā savyaṃ bhūmau pitṛparāyaṇaḥ //
2.11.d:
सदा सर्पिस्तिलैर्युक्तांस्त्रीन्पिण्डान्निर्वपेद्भुवि ।
जानु कृत्वा तथा सव्यं भूमौ पितृपरायणः ॥
2.11.m: He should always deposit three rice-balls mixed with ghee and sesame seeds on the ground, / having likewise placed his left knee on the ground, devoted to the ancestors.

2.11.s:
pitṝnpitāmahāṃścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahān /
āhūya ca pitṝnprāñcaḥ pitṛtīrthena yatnataḥ //
2.11.d:
पितॄन्पितामहांश्चैव तथैव प्रपितामहान् ।
आहूय च पितॄन्प्राञ्चः पितृतीर्थेन यत्नतः ॥
2.11.m: Having invoked the fathers, the grandfathers, and likewise the great-grandfathers, / facing eastward, with effort through the tīrtha of the ancestors,

2.11.s:
piṇḍānparikṣipetsamyagapasavyamatandritaḥ /
annādyaireva mukhyaiścabhakṣyaiścaiva pṛthagvidhaiḥ //
2.11.d:
पिण्डान्परिक्षिपेत्सम्यगपसव्यमतन्द्रितः ।
अन्नाद्यैरेव मुख्यैश्चभक्ष्यैश्चैव पृथग्विधैः ॥
2.11.m: with sacred thread over the right shoulder and unwearied, he should properly scatter the rice-balls, / along with the foremost food and various kinds of edibles.

2.11.s:
pṛthaṅmātāmahānāṃ tu kecidicchanti mānavāḥ /
trīnpiṇḍānānupūrvyeṇa sāṃguṣṭhānpuṣṭivarddhanān //
2.11.d:
पृथङ्मातामहानां तु केचिदिच्छन्ति मानवाः ।
त्रीन्पिण्डानानुपूर्व्येण सांगुष्ठान्पुष्टिवर्द्धनान् ॥
2.11.m: Some men, however, desire separately for the maternal grandfathers / three rice-balls in order, measuring the size of a thumb, that increase prosperity.

2.11.s:
jānvantarābhyāṃ yatnena piṇḍāndadyādyathākramam /
savyottarābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ dhārārthaṃ mantramuccaran //
2.11.d:
जान्वन्तराभ्यां यत्नेन पिण्डान्दद्याद्यथाक्रमम् ।
सव्योत्तराभ्यां पाणिभ्यां धारार्थं मन्त्रमुच्चरन् ॥
2.11.m: With effort he should offer the rice-balls in order between his knees, / with both hands, the left placed above, reciting the mantra for the pouring of water.

2.11.s:
namo vaḥ pitaraḥ śoṣāyeti sarvamatandritaḥ /
dakṣiṇasyāṃ tu pāṇibhyāṃ prathamaṃ piṇḍamutsṛjet //
2.11.d:
नमो वः पितरः शोषायेति सर्वमतन्द्रितः ।
दक्षिणस्यां तु पाणिभ्यां प्रथमं पिण्डमुत्सृजेत् ॥
2.11.m: Reciting entirely without fatigue: 'Homage to you, O ancestors, for vigor,' / he should offer the first rice-ball with his right hand.

2.11.s:
namo vaḥ pitaraḥ saumyaḥ paṭhannevamatandritaḥ /
savyottarābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ dharmer'dhaṃ samatandritaḥ //
2.11.d:
नमो वः पितरः सौम्यः पठन्नेवमतन्द्रितः ।
सव्योत्तराभ्यां पाणिभ्यां धर्मेर्ऽधं समतन्द्रितः ॥
2.11.m: Reciting without fatigue: 'Homage to you, O ancestors, who are Soma-drinking,' / with both hands, the left placed above, completely unwearied according to duty,

2.11.s:
ulūkhalasya lekhāyāmudapātrāvasecanam /
kṣaumaṃ sūtraṃ navaṃ dadyācchāṇaṃ kārpāsakaṃ tathā //
2.11.d:
उलूखलस्य लेखायामुदपात्रावसेचनम् ।
क्षौमं सूत्रं नवं दद्याच्छाणं कार्पासकं तथा ॥
2.11.m: he should pour out the water-vessel in the line of the mortar. / He should offer new linen thread, or hempen, or cotton.

2.11.s:
patrorṇaṃ paṭṭasūtraṃ ca kauśeyaṃ parivarjayet /
varjayedyakṣaṇaṃ yajñe yadyapyahatavastrajām //
2.11.d:
पत्रोर्णं पट्टसूत्रं च कौशेयं परिवर्जयेत् ।
वर्जयेद्यक्षणं यज्ञे यद्यप्यहतवस्त्रजाम् ॥
2.11.m: He should avoid bleached silk, woven silk, and silk fabric; / he should avoid what is injured in the rite, even if produced from unwashed cloth.

2.11.s:
na prīṇanti tathaitāni dātu ścāpyahitaṃ bhavet /
śreṣṭhamāhustrikakudamañjanaṃ nityameva ca //
2.11.d:
न प्रीणन्ति तथैतानि दातु श्चाप्यहितं भवेत् ।
श्रेष्ठमाहुस्त्रिककुदमञ्जनं नित्यमेव च ॥
2.11.m: These do not please [them], and it would bring misfortune to the giver. / They declare that collyrium from Mount Trikakud is always the best,

2.11.s:
kṛṣṇebhyaśca telaistailaṃ yatnātsuparirakṣitam /
candanāguruṇī cobhe tamālośīrapadmakam //
2.11.d:
कृष्णेभ्यश्च तेलैस्तैलं यत्नात्सुपरिरक्षितम् ।
चन्दनागुरुणी चोभे तमालोशीरपद्मकम् ॥
2.11.m: and oil diligently preserved from black sesame seeds; / both sandalwood and aloe-wood, tamāla, uśīra, and padmaka;

2.11.s:
dhūpaśca guggalaḥ śreṣṭasturuṣkaḥ śveta eva ca /
śuklāḥ sumanasaḥ śreṣṭhāstathā padmotpalāni ca //
2.11.d:
धूपश्च गुग्गलः श्रेष्टस्तुरुष्कः श्वेत एव च ।
शुक्लाः सुमनसः श्रेष्ठास्तथा पद्मोत्पलानि च ॥
2.11.m: and as incense, bdellium is best, as well as white turuṣka; / white flowers are best, and likewise blue and pink lotuses,

2.11.s:
gandharūpopapannāni cāraṇyāni ca kṛtsnaśaḥ /
tathā hi sumanā nāḍīrūpikāsmakuraṇḍikā //
2.11.d:
गन्धरूपोपपन्नानि चारण्यानि च कृत्स्नशः ।
तथा हि सुमना नाडीरूपिकास्मकुरण्डिका ॥
2.11.m: and all wild flowers endowed with fragrance and beauty. / However, the jasmine, the nāḍīrūpikā, the asmakuraṇḍikā—

2.11.s:
puṣpāṇi varjanīyāni śrāddhakarmaṇi nityaśaḥ /
yathā gandhādapetāni cogragandhāni yāni ca //
2.11.d:
पुष्पाणि वर्जनीयानि श्राद्धकर्मणि नित्यशः ।
यथा गन्धादपेतानि चोग्रगन्धानि यानि च ॥
2.11.m: these flowers are always to be avoided in the śrāddha rite; / likewise those devoid of fragrance and those that have a pungent odor.

2.11.s:
varjanīyāni puṣpāṇi puṣṭimanviccatā sadā /
dvijātayo yathoddiṣṭā niyatāḥ syurudaṅmukhāḥ //
2.11.d:
वर्जनीयानि पुष्पाणि पुष्टिमन्विच्चता सदा ।
द्विजातयो यथोद्दिष्टा नियताः स्युरुदङ्मुखाः ॥
2.11.m: Flowers are always to be avoided by one who desires prosperity. / As prescribed, the twice-born should be restrained and face north.

2.11.s:
pūjayedyajamānastu vidhivadyakṣiṇāmukhaḥ /
teṣāmabhimukho dadyāddarbhatpiṇḍāṃśca yatnataḥ //
2.11.d:
पूजयेद्यजमानस्तु विधिवद्यक्षिणामुखः ।
तेषामभिमुखो दद्याद्दर्भत्पिण्डांश्च यत्नतः ॥
2.11.m: The patron of the sacrifice, facing south, should worship according to rule. / Facing them, he should diligently offer the darbha grass and the rice-balls.

2.11.s:
anena vidhinā sākṣādarcitāḥ syuḥ pitāmahāḥ /
haritā vai sa piñjālāḥ puṣṭāḥ snigdhāḥ samāhitāḥ //
2.11.d:
अनेन विधिना साक्षादर्चिताः स्युः पितामहाः ।
हरिता वै स पिञ्जालाः पुष्टाः स्निग्धाः समाहिताः ॥
2.11.m: By this rule, the grandfathers are directly honored. / Green, yellowish, sturdy, smooth, and well-gathered,

2.11.s:
ratnimātrāḥ pramāṇena vitṛtīrthena saṃsmṛtāḥ /
upamūle tathā nīlā viṣṭarārthaṃ kuśottamāḥ //
2.11.d:
रत्निमात्राः प्रमाणेन वितृतीर्थेन संस्मृताः ।
उपमूले तथा नीला विष्टरार्थं कुशोत्तमाः ॥
2.11.m: measured to the length of a ratni, held by the tīrtha of the ancestors, / and dark near the root, are the excellent kuśa blades for the seat.

2.11.s:
tathā śyāmākanīvārā dūrvā ca samudāhṛtā /
pūrvaṃ kīrttimatāṃ śreṣṭho babhūvāśvaḥ prajāpatiḥ //
2.11.d:
तथा श्यामाकनीवारा दूर्वा च समुदाहृता ।
पूर्वं कीर्त्तिमतां श्रेष्ठो बभूवाश्वः प्रजापतिः ॥
2.11.m: Likewise, wild millets, wild rice, and dūrvā grass are recommended. / Formerly, the best of the renowned, the horse, was Prajāpati;

2.11.s:
tasya bālā nipatitā bhūmau kāśatvāmāgatāḥ /
tasmāddeyāḥ sadā kāśāḥ śrāddhakarmasu pūjitāḥ //
2.11.d:
तस्य बाला निपतिता भूमौ काशत्वामागताः ।
तस्माद्देयाः सदा काशाः श्राद्धकर्मसु पूजिताः ॥
2.11.m: his hairs fell upon the ground and became kāśa grass. / Therefore, kāśa grasses are always to be offered and honored in śrāddha rites.

2.11.s:
piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ teṣu karttavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā /
prajāḥ puṣṭidyutiprajñākīrttikāntisamanvitāḥ //
2.11.d:
पिण्डनिर्वपणं तेषु कर्त्तव्यं भूतिमिच्छता ।
प्रजाः पुष्टिद्युतिप्रज्ञाकीर्त्तिकान्तिसमन्विताः ॥
2.11.m: The offering of rice-balls should be made upon them by one desiring prosperity. / Offspring endowed with strength, splendor, wisdom, fame, and beauty,

2.11.s:
bhavanti rucirā nityaṃ vipāpmāno 'ghavarjitāḥ /
sakṛdevāstaredyarbhānpiṇḍārthe dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ //
2.11.d:
भवन्ति रुचिरा नित्यं विपाप्मानो ऽघवर्जिताः ।
सकृदेवास्तरेद्यर्भान्पिण्डार्थे दक्षिणामुखः ॥
2.11.m: ever charming, free from evil, and devoid of sin, come to be. / Facing south, he should spread darbha grass only once for the rice-balls,

2.11.s:
prāgdakṣiṇāgrānniyato vidhi cāpyatra vakṣyati /
na dīno nāpi vā kruddho na caivānyamanā naraḥ /
ekatra cādhāya manaḥ śrāddhaṃ kuryātsamāhitaḥ //
2.11.d:
प्राग्दक्षिणाग्रान्नियतो विधि चाप्यत्र वक्ष्यति ।
न दीनो नापि वा क्रुद्धो न चैवान्यमना नरः ।
एकत्र चाधाय मनः श्राद्धं कुर्यात्समाहितः ॥
2.11.m: with tips directed to the south-east, restrained; and here the rule will declare: / A man, not depressed, nor angry, nor absent-minded, / concentrating his mind on one point, should perform the śrāddha with composed attention.

2.11.s:
nihanmi sarvaṃ yadamedhyavadbhaveddhataśca sarve suradānavā mayā /
rakṣāṃsi yakṣāḥ sapiśācasaṃghā hatā mayā yātudhānāśca sarve //
2.11.d:
निहन्मि सर्वं यदमेध्यवद्भवेद्धतश्च सर्वे सुरदानवा मया ।
रक्षांसि यक्षाः सपिशाचसंघा हता मया यातुधानाश्च सर्वे ॥
2.11.m: "I destroy whatever is impure; all the gods and Dānavas have been struck down by me; / the Rakṣases, Yakṣas, along with the hosts of Piśācas, have been slain by me, and all the Yātudhānas."

2.11.s:
etena mantreṇa tu saṃyatātmā tāṃ vai vediṃ sakṛdullikhya dhīraḥ /
śivāṃ hi buddhiṃ dhruvamicchamānaḥ kṣipeddvicātirdiśamuttarāṃ gataḥ //
2.11.d:
एतेन मन्त्रेण तु संयतात्मा तां वै वेदिं सकृदुल्लिख्य धीरः ।
शिवां हि बुद्धिं ध्रुवमिच्छमानः क्षिपेद्द्विचातिर्दिशमुत्तरां गतः ॥
2.11.m: With this mantra, self-restrained, the steadfast man, having inscribed that altar once, / desiring auspicious and enduring wisdom, turning to the north, should toss [the implement].

2.11.s:
evaṃ pitryaṃ dṛṣṭamantraṃ hi yasyatasyāsurā varjayantīha sarve /
yasmindeśe paṭhyate mantra eṣa taṃ vai deśaṃ rākṣasā varjayanti //
2.11.d:
एवं पित्र्यं दृष्टमन्त्रं हि यस्यतस्यासुरा वर्जयन्तीह सर्वे ।
यस्मिन्देशे पठ्यते मन्त्र एष तं वै देशं राक्षसा वर्जयन्ति ॥
2.11.m: Indeed, all the Asuras avoid the rite of him whose ancestral mantra is thus seen; / the Rākṣasas shun that region in which this mantra is recited.

2.11.s:
annaprakārānaśucīnasādhūnsaṃvīkṣate no spṛśaṃśvāpi dadyāt /
pavitrapāṇiśca bhavenna vā hi yaḥ pumānna kāryasya phalaṃ samaśnute //
2.11.d:
अन्नप्रकारानशुचीनसाधून्संवीक्षते नो स्पृशंश्वापि दद्यात् ।
पवित्रपाणिश्च भवेन्न वा हि यः पुमान्न कार्यस्य फलं समश्नुते ॥
2.11.m: If a man looks upon impure, improper varieties of food, or touches them while giving, / or if he does not hold a purifier in his hand, he does not obtain the fruit of the rite.

2.11.s:
anena vidhinā nityaṃ śrāddhaṃ kuryāddhi yaḥ sadā /
manasā kāṅkṣate yadyattattadyadyuḥ pitamahāḥ //
2.11.d:
अनेन विधिना नित्यं श्राद्धं कुर्याद्धि यः सदा ।
मनसा काङ्क्षते यद्यत्तत्तद्यद्युः पितमहाः ॥
2.11.m: Whoever constantly performs the śrāddha always according to this procedure, / whatever he desires in his mind, that the grandfathers bestow.

2.11.s:
pitaro hṛṣṭamanaso rakṣāṃsi vimanāṃsi ca /
bhavantyevaṃ kṛte śrāddhe nityameva prayatnataḥ //
2.11.d:
पितरो हृष्टमनसो रक्षांसि विमनांसि च ।
भवन्त्येवं कृते श्राद्धे नित्यमेव प्रयत्नतः ॥
2.11.m: The ancestors become delighted in mind and the Rakṣases dispirited / when the śrāddha is performed in this manner always with diligence.

2.11.s:
śūdrāḥ śrāddheṣvavikṣīraṃ balvajā upalāstathā /
viraṇāścotuvālāśca laḍvā varjyāśca nityaśaḥ //
2.11.d:
शूद्राः श्राद्धेष्वविक्षीरं बल्वजा उपलास्तथा ।
विरणाश्चोतुवालाश्च लड्वा वर्ज्याश्च नित्यशः ॥
2.11.m: Śūdras at śrāddhas, sheep's milk, balvaja grass, stones, / viraṇa grass, utuvāla grass, and laḍva grass are always to be avoided.

2.11.s:
evamādīnyayajñāni tṛṇāni parivarjayet /
añjanābhyajanaṃ gandhānsūtrapraṇayanaṃ tathā //
2.11.d:
एवमादीन्ययज्ञानि तृणानि परिवर्जयेत् ।
अञ्जनाभ्यजनं गन्धान्सूत्रप्रणयनं तथा ॥
2.11.m: One should avoid grasses unfit for sacrifice such as these. / Collyrium, ointments, perfumes, and the presenting of the thread,

2.11.s:
kāśeḥ punarbhavaiḥ kāryamaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet /
kāśāḥ punarbhavā ye ca barhiṇo hyupabarhiṇaḥ //
2.11.d:
काशेः पुनर्भवैः कार्यमश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ।
काशाः पुनर्भवा ये च बर्हिणो ह्युपबर्हिणः ॥
2.11.m: should be performed with fresh shoots of kāśa grass; he obtains the fruit of an horse sacrifice. / The fresh kāśa shoots are the barhis and the upabarhis.

2.11.s:
ityete pitaro devā devāśca pitaraḥ punaḥ /
puṣpagandhavibhūṣāṇāmeṣa mantra udāhṛtaḥ //
2.11.d:
इत्येते पितरो देवा देवाश्च पितरः पुनः ।
पुष्पगन्धविभूषाणामेष मन्त्र उदाहृतः ॥
2.11.m: Thus these ancestors are gods, and the gods again are ancestors. / This mantra is declared for flowers, perfumes, and adornments.

2.11.s:
āhṛtya dakṣiṇāgniṃ tu homārthaṃ vai prayatnataḥ /
anyārthe laukikaṃ vāpi juhuyātkarmasiddhaye //
2.11.d:
आहृत्य दक्षिणाग्निं तु होमार्थं वै प्रयत्नतः ।
अन्यार्थे लौकिकं वापि जुहुयात्कर्मसिद्धये ॥
2.11.m: Having brought the dakṣiṇāgni fire with effort for the sake of the oblation, / or a secular fire for another purpose, he should offer oblations for the success of the rite.

2.11.s:
antarvidhāya samidhastato dīpto vidhīyate /
samāhitena manasā praṇīyāgniṃ samantataḥ //
2.11.d:
अन्तर्विधाय समिधस्ततो दीप्तो विधीयते ।
समाहितेन मनसा प्रणीयाग्निं समन्ततः ॥
2.11.m: Having placed fuel sticks within, the flame is then kindled, / having led the fire in every direction with a collected mind.

2.11.s:
agnaye kavyavāhāya svadhā aṅgirase namaḥ /
somāya vai pitṛmate svadhā aṅgirase punaḥ //
2.11.d:
अग्नये कव्यवाहाय स्वधा अङ्गिरसे नमः ।
सोमाय वै पितृमते स्वधा अङ्गिरसे पुनः ॥
2.11.m: “To Agni, bearer of ancestral offerings, svadhā; to Aṅgiras, obeisance. / To Soma, accompanied by the ancestors, svadhā; to Aṅgiras again.

2.11.s:
yamāya vaivasvataye svadhānama iti dhruvam /
ityete homamantrāstu trayāṇāmanupūrvaśaḥ //
2.11.d:
यमाय वैवस्वतये स्वधानम इति ध्रुवम् ।
इत्येते होममन्त्रास्तु त्रयाणामनुपूर्वशः ॥
2.11.m: To Yama Vaivasvata, svadhā, obeisance,” thus surely [it is spoken]. / These indeed are the oblational formulas for the three, in successive order.

2.11.s:
dakṣiṇenāgnaye nityaṃ somāyottaratastathā /
etayorantare nityaṃ juhuyādvai vivasvate //
2.11.d:
दक्षिणेनाग्नये नित्यं सोमायोत्तरतस्तथा ।
एतयोरन्तरे नित्यं जुहुयाद्वै विवस्वते ॥
2.11.m: Always to Agni on the south, and likewise to Soma on the north; / between these two he should always offer indeed unto Vivasvat.

2.11.s:
upahāraḥ svadhākārastathaivollekhanaṃ ca yat /
homajapye namaskāraḥ prokṣaṇaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ //
2.11.d:
उपहारः स्वधाकारस्तथैवोल्लेखनं च यत् ।
होमजप्ये नमस्कारः प्रोक्षणं च विशेषतः ॥
2.11.m: The presentation of offerings, the utterance of “svadhā”, and likewise the furrowing [of the ground], / the obeisance in oblations and muttered prayers, and especially the sprinkling [of water],

2.11.s:
bahuhavyendhane cāgnau susamiddhe tathaiva ca /
añjanābyañjanaṃ caiva piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ tathā //
2.11.d:
बहुहव्येन्धने चाग्नौ सुसमिद्धे तथैव च ।
अञ्जनाब्यञ्जनं चैव पिण्डनिर्वपणं तथा ॥
2.11.m: and when the fire has abundant fuel for offerings and is well kindled, / the anointing and smearing, as well as the offering of piṇḍas—

2.11.s:
aśvamedhaphalaṃ caitatsamiddhe yatkṛtaṃ dvijaiḥ /
kriyā sarvā yathoddiṣṭāḥ prayatnena samācaret //
2.11.d:
अश्वमेधफलं चैतत्समिद्धे यत्कृतं द्विजैः ।
क्रिया सर्वा यथोद्दिष्टाः प्रयत्नेन समाचरेत् ॥
2.11.m: this [brings] the fruit of a horse sacrifice when performed by twice-born men in a well-kindled [fire]. / One should perform with effort all the rites as prescribed.

2.11.s:
bahuhavyendhane cāgnau susamiddhe viśeṣataḥ /
vidhūme lelihāne ca hotavyaṃ karmasiddhaye //
2.11.d:
बहुहव्येन्धने चाग्नौ सुसमिद्धे विशेषतः ।
विधूमे लेलिहाने च होतव्यं कर्मसिद्धये ॥
2.11.m: In a fire with abundant fuel for offerings, and especially well kindled, / free of smoke and licking up [the fuel], one must offer for the success of the rite.

2.11.s:
aprabuddhe samiddhe vā juhuyādyo hutāśane /
yajamāno bhave dandhaḥ so 'mutreti hi naḥ śrutam //
2.11.d:
अप्रबुद्धे समिद्धे वा जुहुयाद्यो हुताशने ।
यजमानो भवे दन्धः सो ऽमुत्रेति हि नः श्रुतम् ॥
2.11.m: If someone should offer in a fire that is unignited or [improperly] kindled, / that sacrificer becomes blind in the next world; so indeed it has been heard by us.

2.11.s:
alpendhano vā rūkṣo 'gnirvasphuliṅgaśca sarvaśaḥ /
jvālādhūmāpasavyaśca sa tu vahnirasiddhaye //
2.11.d:
अल्पेन्धनो वा रूक्षो ऽग्निर्वस्फुलिङ्गश्च सर्वशः ।
ज्वालाधूमापसव्यश्च स तु वह्निरसिद्धये ॥
2.11.m: A fire with little fuel, or rough, emitting sparks on all sides, / whose flames and smoke turn counter-clockwise, leads to failure of the rite.

2.11.s:
durgandhaścaiva nīlaśca kṛṣṇaścaiva viśeṣataḥ /
bhūmiṃ vagāhate yatra tatra vidyātparābhavat //
2.11.d:
दुर्गन्धश्चैव नीलश्च कृष्णश्चैव विशेषतः ।
भूमिं वगाहते यत्र तत्र विद्यात्पराभवत् ॥
2.11.m: That which is foul-smelling, and especially blue or black, / wherever it enters the ground, one should know that defeat [will follow].

2.11.s:
arciṣmān piṇḍitaśikhaḥ sarppikāñjanasannibhaḥ /
snigdhaḥ pradakṣiṇaścaiva vahniḥ syātkāryasiddhaye //
2.11.d:
अर्चिष्मान् पिण्डितशिखः सर्प्पिकाञ्जनसन्निभः ।
स्निग्धः प्रदक्षिणश्चैव वह्निः स्यात्कार्यसिद्धये ॥
2.11.m: Radiant, with bunched flames, resembling ghee or collyrium, / smooth and turning clockwise, such a fire brings success in one’s undertaking.

2.11.s:
naranārīgaṇebhyaśca pūjāṃ prāpnoti śāśvatīm /
akṣayaṃ pūjitāstena bhavanti pitaro 'gnayaḥ //
2.11.d:
नरनारीगणेभ्यश्च पूजां प्राप्नोति शाश्वतीम् ।
अक्षयं पूजितास्तेन भवन्ति पितरो ऽग्नयः ॥
2.11.m: And he attains everlasting worship from groups of men and women; / through him the ancestors and the fires become imperishably worshipped.

2.11.s:
bilvoduṃbarapatrāṇi phalāni samidhastathā /
śrāddhe mahāpavitrāṇi medhyāni ca viśeṣataḥ //
2.11.d:
बिल्वोदुंबरपत्राणि फलानि समिधस्तथा ।
श्राद्धे महापवित्राणि मेध्यानि च विशेषतः ॥
2.11.m: Leaves of the bilva and uḍumbara, fruits, and likewise fuel sticks / are supremely purifying in a śrāddha, and especially pure for sacrificial rites.

2.11.s:
pavitraṃ ca dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ śuddhaye janmakarmaṇām /
pātreṣu phalamuddiṣṭaṃ yanmayā śrāddhakarmaṇi //
2.11.d:
पवित्रं च द्विजश्रेष्ठाः शुद्धये जन्मकर्मणाम् ।
पात्रेषु फलमुद्दिष्टं यन्मया श्राद्धकर्मणि ॥
2.11.m: A strainer, O best of the twice-born, [is used] for the purification of rites from birth; / whatever fruit was described by me with regard to the vessels in the śrāddha rite,

2.11.s:
tadeva kṛtsnaṃ vijñeyaṃ samitsu ca yathākramam /
kṛtvā samāhitaṃ cittamāgneyaṃ vai karomyaham //
2.11.d:
तदेव कृत्स्नं विज्ञेयं समित्सु च यथाक्रमम् ।
कृत्वा समाहितं चित्तमाग्नेयं वै करोम्यहम् ॥
2.11.m: all that should be understood to apply to the fuel sticks as well in due order. / Having composed his mind, [he says,] “I shall indeed perform the rite to Agni.”

2.11.s:
anujñātaḥ kuruṣveti tathaiva dvijasattamaiḥ /
ghṛtamādāya pātre ca juhuyāddhavyavāhane //
2.11.d:
अनुज्ञातः कुरुष्वेति तथैव द्विजसत्तमैः ।
घृतमादाय पात्रे च जुहुयाद्धव्यवाहने ॥
2.11.m: Permitted with “Perform [it]” in the same way by the best of the twice-born, / taking ghee in the vessel, he should offer into the fire.

2.11.s:
palāśaplakṣanyagrodhaplakṣāśvatthavikaṅkatāḥ /
uduṃbarastathābilvaścandano yajñiyāśca ye //
2.11.d:
पलाशप्लक्षन्यग्रोधप्लक्षाश्वत्थविकङ्कताः ।
उदुंबरस्तथाबिल्वश्चन्दनो यज्ञियाश्च ये ॥
2.11.m: Palāśa, plakṣa, nyagrodha, aśvattha, vikaṅkata, / uḍumbara, and likewise bilva, sandalwood, and whichever trees are fit for sacrifice,

2.11.s:
saralo devadāruśca śālaśca kadirastathā /
samidarthe praśastāḥ syurete vṛkṣā viśeṣataḥ //
2.11.d:
सरलो देवदारुश्च शालश्च कदिरस्तथा ।
समिदर्थे प्रशस्ताः स्युरेते वृक्षा विशेषतः ॥
2.11.m: sarala, devadāru, śāla, and likewise khadira— / these trees are especially praiseworthy for the purpose of fuel sticks.

2.11.s:
grāmyāḥ kaṇṭakinaścaiva yājñiyā ye ca kecana /
pūjitāḥ samidarthaṃ te pitṝṇāṃ vacanaṃ yathā //
2.11.d:
ग्राम्याः कण्टकिनश्चैव याज्ञिया ये च केचन ।
पूजिताः समिदर्थं ते पितॄणां वचनं यथा ॥
2.11.m: Those that grow in villages, those with thorns, and whichever are fit for sacrifice, / they are praised for the purpose of fuel sticks according to the word of the ancestors.

2.11.s:
samidbhiḥ ṣaṭphaleyābhirjuhuyādyo hutāśanam /
phalaṃ yatkarmaṇastasya tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu //
2.11.d:
समिद्भिः षट्फलेयाभिर्जुहुयाद्यो हुताशनम् ।
फलं यत्कर्मणस्तस्य तन्मे निगदतः शृणु ॥
2.11.m: He who offers into the fire with fuel sticks yielding the six kinds of fruit— / hear from me as I declare the fruit of his action.

2.11.s:
akṣayaṃ sarvakāmīyamaśvamedhaphalaṃ hi tat /
śleṣmāntako naktamālaḥ kapitthaḥ śālmalistathā //
2.11.d:
अक्षयं सर्वकामीयमश्वमेधफलं हि तत् ।
श्लेष्मान्तको नक्तमालः कपित्थः शाल्मलिस्तथा ॥
2.11.m: It is imperishable, granting all desires, indeed the fruit of a horse sacrifice. / Śleṣmātaka, naktamāla, kapittha, and likewise śālmali,

2.11.s:
nīpo vibhītakaścaiva śrāddhakarmaṇi garhitāḥ /
cirabilvastathā kolastidukaḥ śrāddhakarmaṇi //
2.11.d:
नीपो विभीतकश्चैव श्राद्धकर्मणि गर्हिताः ।
चिरबिल्वस्तथा कोलस्तिदुकः श्राद्धकर्मणि ॥
2.11.m: nīpa and vibhītaka are condemned in the śrāddha rite; / cirabilva, likewise kola, and tinduka in the śrāddha rite,

2.11.s:
balvajaḥ kovidāraśca varjanīyāḥ samantataḥ /
śakunānāṃ nivāsāṃśca varjayeta mahīruhān //
2.11.d:
बल्वजः कोविदारश्च वर्जनीयाः समन्ततः ।
शकुनानां निवासांश्च वर्जयेत महीरुहान् ॥
2.11.m: balvaja and kovidāra are to be avoided entirely; / and one should avoid trees that are dwellings of birds,

2.11.s:
anyāṃścaivaṃvidhānsarvānnayajñīyāṃśca varjayet /
svadheti caiva mantrāṇāṃ pitṝṇāṃ vacanaṃ yathā /
svāheti caiva devānāṃ yajñakarmaṇyudāhṛtam //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīye
upoddhātapāde śrāddhakalpe samidvarṇana nāmaikādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ // 11//
2.11.d:
अन्यांश्चैवंविधान्सर्वान्नयज्ञीयांश्च वर्जयेत् ।
स्वधेति चैव मन्त्राणां पितॄणां वचनं यथा ।
स्वाहेति चैव देवानां यज्ञकर्मण्युदाहृतम् ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीये
उपोद्धातपादे श्राद्धकल्पे समिद्वर्णन नामैकादशो ऽध्यायः ॥ 11॥
2.11.m:
and all other such [trees] that are unfit for sacrifice should be avoided. / “Svadhā” is prescribed for the mantras of the ancestors, / while “svāhā” is uttered for the gods in the sacrificial rite.

Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled “Description of Fuel Sticks,” in the Rite of Ancestral Offerings in the Upoddhātapāda, the third middle section of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa proclaimed by Vāyu.

2.12.s:
sūta uvāca
devāścapitaraścaiva anyonyaṃ niyatāḥ smṛtāḥ /
ātharvaṇastveṣa vidhirityuvāca bṛhaspatiḥ //
2.12.d:
सूत उवाच
देवाश्चपितरश्चैव अन्योन्यं नियताः स्मृताः ।
आथर्वणस्त्वेष विधिरित्युवाच बृहस्पतिः ॥
2.12.m: The bard said: / The gods and the ancestors are traditionally remembered as interdependent. / This is indeed the rule of the Atharvans; so spoke Bṛhaspati.

2.12.s:
pūjayeta pitṝnpūrvaṃ devāṃśca tadanantaram /
devā api pitṝnpūrvamarccayanti hi yatnataḥ //
2.12.d:
पूजयेत पितॄन्पूर्वं देवांश्च तदनन्तरम् ।
देवा अपि पितॄन्पूर्वमर्च्चयन्ति हि यत्नतः ॥
2.12.m: One should worship the ancestors first, and the gods immediately thereafter. / Even the gods diligently worship the ancestors first.

2.12.s:
dakṣasya duhitā nāmnā viśvā nāmeti viśrutā /
viśvākhyāstu sutāstasyāṃ dharmato jajñire daśa //
2.12.d:
दक्षस्य दुहिता नाम्ना विश्वा नामेति विश्रुता ।
विश्वाख्यास्तु सुतास्तस्यां धर्मतो जज्ञिरे दश ॥
2.12.m: There was a daughter of Dakṣa, renowned by the name Viśvā; / through Dharma, ten sons known as the Viśvas were born from her.

2.12.s:
prakhyātā striṣu lokeṣu sarvalokanamaskṛtāḥ /
samastāste mahātmānaścerurugraṃ mahattapaḥ //
2.12.d:
प्रख्याता स्त्रिषु लोकेषु सर्वलोकनमस्कृताः ।
समस्तास्ते महात्मानश्चेरुरुग्रं महत्तपः ॥
2.12.m: Famed in the three worlds, bowed to by all the worlds, / all those great-souled ones performed fierce, severe austerities.

2.12.s:
himavacchikhare ramye devarṣigaṇasevite /
śuddhena mansā prītā ūcustānpitarastadā //
2.12.d:
हिमवच्छिखरे रम्ये देवर्षिगणसेविते ।
शुद्धेन मन्सा प्रीता ऊचुस्तान्पितरस्तदा ॥
2.12.m: On a delightful peak of the Himālaya, frequented by hosts of divine seers, / the ancestors, pleased with pure minds, then spoke to them:

2.12.s:
varaṃ vṛṇīdhvaṃ prītāḥ sma kaṃ kāmaṃ kakhāmahe /
evamukte tu pitṛbhistadā trailokyabhāvanaḥ //
2.12.d:
वरं वृणीध्वं प्रीताः स्म कं कामं कखामहे ।
एवमुक्ते तु पितृभिस्तदा त्रैलोक्यभावनः ॥
2.12.m: “Choose a boon! We are pleased; what desire shall we fulfill?” / When spoken to thus by the ancestors, then the creator of the three worlds,

2.12.s:
brahmovāca mahātejāstapasā taistu toṣitaḥ /
prīto 'smi tapasānena kaṃ kāmaṃ karavāṇi vaḥ //
2.12.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच महातेजास्तपसा तैस्तु तोषितः ।
प्रीतो ऽस्मि तपसानेन कं कामं करवाणि वः ॥
2.12.m: Brahmā of great splendor, delighted by their austerities, spoke: / “I am pleased with this austerity; what desire shall I fulfill for you?”

2.12.s:
evamuktāstadā viśve brahmaṇā viśvakarmaṇā /
ūcuste sahitāḥ sarve brahmāṇāṃ lokabhāvanam //
2.12.d:
एवमुक्तास्तदा विश्वे ब्रह्मणा विश्वकर्मणा ।
ऊचुस्ते सहिताः सर्वे ब्रह्माणां लोकभावनम् ॥
2.12.m: Addressed thus at that time by Brahmā, the maker of the universe, / all the Viśvas together said to Brahmā, the creator of the worlds:

2.12.s:
śrāddhe 'smākaṃ bhavedaṃśo hyeṣa naḥ kāṅkṣito varaḥ /
pratyuvāca tato brahmā tānvai tridaśapūjitaḥ //
2.12.d:
श्राद्धे ऽस्माकं भवेदंशो ह्येष नः काङ्क्षितो वरः ।
प्रत्युवाच ततो ब्रह्मा तान्वै त्रिदशपूजितः ॥
2.12.m: “May there be a share for us in the śrāddha; this is the boon we desire.” / Then Brahmā, worshipped by the gods, replied to them:

2.12.s:
bhaviṣyatyevamevaṃ tu kāṅkṣito vo varastu yaḥ /
pitṛbhiśca tathetyuktamevametanna saṃśayaḥ //
2.12.d:
भविष्यत्येवमेवं तु काङ्क्षितो वो वरस्तु यः ।
पितृभिश्च तथेत्युक्तमेवमेतन्न संशयः ॥
2.12.m: “It shall be just so, this boon desired by you.” / And by the ancestors it was said, “So be it; thus it is, without doubt.”

2.12.s:
sahasmābhistu bhoktavyaṃ yatkiṃ ciddṛśyate tviha /
asmākaṃ kalpite śrāddhe yuṣmānaprāśanaṃ hi vai //
bhaviṣyati manuṣyeṣu satyame tadbruvāmahe /
mālyairgandhaistathānnena yuṣmānagre 'rccayiṣyati /1 12.12//
2.12.d:
सहस्माभिस्तु भोक्तव्यं यत्किं चिद्दृश्यते त्विह ।
अस्माकं कल्पिते श्राद्धे युष्मानप्राशनं हि वै ॥
भविष्यति मनुष्येषु सत्यमे तद्ब्रुवामहे ।
माल्यैर्गन्धैस्तथान्नेन युष्मानग्रे ऽर्च्चयिष्यति ।1 12.12॥
2.12.m:
[The ancestors said:] “Whatever is seen here must be enjoyed together with us. / In the śrāddha arranged for us, your non-eating [is impossible].

This will happen among men; we speak this truth: / with garlands, perfumes, and food, one will worship you first.

2.12.s:
agre dattvā tu yuṣmākamasmākaṃ dāsyate tataḥ /
visarjanamathāsmākaṃ pūrvaṃ paścāttu daivatam //
2.12.d:
अग्रे दत्त्वा तु युष्माकमस्माकं दास्यते ततः ।
विसर्जनमथास्माकं पूर्वं पश्चात्तु दैवतम् ॥
2.12.m: Having given to you first, it will then be given to us. / Then the dismissal will be ours first, and the divine one afterwards.

2.12.s:
rakṣaṇaṃ caiva śrāddhasya ātithyasya vidhidvayam /
bhūtānāṃ devatānāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ caiva karmaṇi //
2.12.d:
रक्षणं चैव श्राद्धस्य आतिथ्यस्य विधिद्वयम् ।
भूतानां देवतानां च पितॄणां चैव कर्मणि ॥
2.12.m: Protection of the śrāddha and the two-fold rule of hospitality / [are established] in the rite for living beings, deities, and ancestors.

2.12.s:
evaṃ kṛte samyagetatsarvameva bhaviṣyati /
evaṃ dattvā varaṃ teṣāṃ brahmā pitṛgaṇaiḥ saha //
2.12.d:
एवं कृते सम्यगेतत्सर्वमेव भविष्यति ।
एवं दत्त्वा वरं तेषां ब्रह्मा पितृगणैः सह ॥
2.12.m: When this is performed thus properly, everything will come to pass.” / Having thus granted a boon to them, Brahmā, along with the groups of ancestors,

2.12.s:
kṣamānugrahakṛddevaḥ saṃcakāra yathoditam /
vede pañca mahāyajñā narāṇāṃ samudāhṛtāḥ //
2.12.d:
क्षमानुग्रहकृद्देवः संचकार यथोदितम् ।
वेदे पञ्च महायज्ञा नराणां समुदाहृताः ॥
2.12.m: the god who bestows forbearance and grace, concluded as prescribed. / In the Veda, five great sacrifices are proclaimed for men.

2.12.s:
etānpañca mahāyajñānnirvapetsatataṃ naraḥ /
yatra sthāsyanti dātārastatsthānaṃ vai nibodhata //
2.12.d:
एतान्पञ्च महायज्ञान्निर्वपेत्सततं नरः ।
यत्र स्थास्यन्ति दातारस्तत्स्थानं वै निबोधत ॥
2.12.m: A man should constantly offer these five great sacrifices. / Understand that abode where the givers will dwell:

2.12.s:
nirbhayaṃ virajaskaṃ ca niḥśokaṃ nirvyathaklamam /
brāhmaṃ sthānamavāpnoti sarvalokapuraskṛtam //
2.12.d:
निर्भयं विरजस्कं च निःशोकं निर्व्यथक्लमम् ।
ब्राह्मं स्थानमवाप्नोति सर्वलोकपुरस्कृतम् ॥
2.12.m: free from fear, free from rajas, sorrowless, free from pain and exhaustion, / he attains the realm of Brahmā, honored by all the worlds.

2.12.s:
śūdreṇāpi ca karttavyāḥ pañcaite mantravarjitāḥ /
ato 'nyathā tu yo bhuṅkte sa ṛṇaṃ nityamaśnute //
2.12.d:
शूद्रेणापि च कर्त्तव्याः पञ्चैते मन्त्रवर्जिताः ।
अतो ऽन्यथा तु यो भुङ्क्ते स ऋणं नित्यमश्नुते ॥
2.12.m: These five must also be performed by a Śūdra, [though] devoid of mantras. / He who eats otherwise always incurs a debt.

2.12.s:
ṛṇaṃ bhuṅkte sa pāpātmā yaḥ pacedātmakāraṇāt /
tasmānnirvartayetpañca mahāyajñānsadā budhaḥ //
2.12.d:
ऋणं भुङ्क्ते स पापात्मा यः पचेदात्मकारणात् ।
तस्मान्निर्वर्तयेत्पञ्च महायज्ञान्सदा बुधः ॥
2.12.m: That evil-minded person eats debt who cooks for his own sake; / therefore a wise man should always perform the five great sacrifices.

2.12.s:
udakpūrve baliṃ kuryādudakānte tathaiva ca /
baliṃ suvihitaṃ kuryā duccairuccataraṃ kṣipet //
2.12.d:
उदक्पूर्वे बलिं कुर्यादुदकान्ते तथैव च ।
बलिं सुविहितं कुर्या दुच्चैरुच्चतरं क्षिपेत् ॥
2.12.m: One should offer a bali in the north-east, and likewise near water; / one should present the bali well-prepared, casting it higher and higher.

2.12.s:
paraśṛṅgaṃ gavāṃ mūtraṃ baliṃ sūtraṃ samutkṣipet /
tannivedyo bhavetpiṇḍaḥ pitṝṇāṃ yastu jīvati //
2.12.d:
परशृङ्गं गवां मूत्रं बलिं सूत्रं समुत्क्षिपेत् ।
तन्निवेद्यो भवेत्पिण्डः पितॄणां यस्तु जीवति ॥
2.12.m: He should throw out an animal's horn, cow urine, the bali offering, and the sacred thread. / For the ancestors, that food ball may be offered to one who is alive.

2.12.s:
iṣṭenānnena bhakṣyaiśca bhojayecca yathāvidhi /
nivedyaṃ kecidicchanti jīvantyapi hi yatnataḥ //
2.12.d:
इष्टेनान्नेन भक्ष्यैश्च भोजयेच्च यथाविधि ।
निवेद्यं केचिदिच्छन्ति जीवन्त्यपि हि यत्नतः ॥
2.12.m: He should feed [the brāhmaṇas] with desired foods and edibles according to rule. / Some desire an offering with diligence even while [the father] is alive.

2.12.s:
devadevā mahātmāno hyete pitara ityuta /
icchanti kecidācāryaḥ paścātpiṇḍanivedanam //
2.12.d:
देवदेवा महात्मानो ह्येते पितर इत्युत ।
इच्छन्ति केचिदाचार्यः पश्चात्पिण्डनिवेदनम् ॥
2.12.m: Indeed, these ancestors are great-souled gods of gods. / Some teachers desire the offering of the food balls [to be performed] afterwards,

2.12.s:
pūjanaṃ caiva vipraṇāṃ pūrvameveha nityaśaḥ /
taddhidharmārthakuśalo netyuvāca bṛhasmatiḥ //
2.12.d:
पूजनं चैव विप्रणां पूर्वमेवेह नित्यशः ।
तद्धिधर्मार्थकुशलो नेत्युवाच बृहस्मतिः ॥
2.12.m: and the worshipping of the brāhmaṇas always first in this world. / But Bṛhaspati, skilled in dharma and artha, said, “No;

2.12.s:
pūrvaṃ nivedayetpiṇḍānpaścādviprāṃśca bhojayet /
yogātmāno mahātmānaḥ pitaro yoga saṃbhavāḥ //
2.12.d:
पूर्वं निवेदयेत्पिण्डान्पश्चाद्विप्रांश्च भोजयेत् ।
योगात्मानो महात्मानः पितरो योग संभवाः ॥
2.12.m: one should offer the food balls first, and afterwards feed the brāhmaṇas. / The ancestors are great souls consisting of yoga, born of yoga.

2.12.s:
somamāpyāyayantyete pitaro yogasaṃsthitāḥ /
tasmāddadyācchuciḥ piṇḍānyogebhyastatparāyaṇaḥ //
2.12.d:
सोममाप्याययन्त्येते पितरो योगसंस्थिताः ।
तस्माद्दद्याच्छुचिः पिण्डान्योगेभ्यस्तत्परायणः ॥
2.12.m: Established in yoga, these ancestors cause Soma to swell; / therefore, pure [and] devoted to them, one should give the food balls to the yogins.

2.12.s:
pitṝṇāṃ hi bhavedetatsākṣādiva hutaṃ haviḥ /
brahmaṇānāṃ sahasrasya yogasthaṃ grāsayedyadi //
2.12.d:
पितॄणां हि भवेदेतत्साक्षादिव हुतं हविः ।
ब्रह्मणानां सहस्रस्य योगस्थं ग्रासयेद्यदि ॥
2.12.m: For this becomes directly like an offering of oblation poured into fire for the ancestors. / If, of a thousand brāhmaṇas, one feeds one who is established in yoga,

2.12.s:
yajamānaṃ ca bhoktṝṃś ca naurivāmbhasi tārayet /
asatāṃ pragraho yatra satāṃ caiva vimānatā //
2.12.d:
यजमानं च भोक्तॄंश् च नौरिवाम्भसि तारयेत् ।
असतां प्रग्रहो यत्र सतां चैव विमानता ॥
2.12.m: he delivers the sacrificer and the eaters like a boat on the water. / Where the wicked are honored and the virtuous are disrespected,

2.12.s:
daṇḍo daivakṛtastatra sadyaḥ patati dāruṇaḥ /
itvā mama sadharmāṇaṃ bāliśaṃ yastu bhojayet //
2.12.d:
दण्डो दैवकृतस्तत्र सद्यः पतति दारुणः ।
इत्वा मम सधर्माणं बालिशं यस्तु भोजयेत् ॥
2.12.m: there severe divine punishment falls immediately. / But one who feeds a fool merely because he observes the same dharma as oneself,

2.12.s:
ādikarma samutsṛjya dātā tatra vinaśyati /
piṇḍamagnau sadā dadyadbhogārthī prathamaṃ naraḥ //
2.12.d:
आदिकर्म समुत्सृज्य दाता तत्र विनश्यति ।
पिण्डमग्नौ सदा दद्यद्भोगार्थी प्रथमं नरः ॥
2.12.m: having abandoned the primary ritual, the giver is ruined in that act. / A man seeking enjoyment should always offer the first food ball into the fire;

2.12.s:
dadyātprajārthī yatnena madhyamaṃ mantrapūrvakam /
uttamāṃ kāntimanvicchangoṣu nityaṃ prayacchati //
2.12.d:
दद्यात्प्रजार्थी यत्नेन मध्यमं मन्त्रपूर्वकम् ।
उत्तमां कान्तिमन्विच्छन्गोषु नित्यं प्रयच्छति ॥
2.12.m: one seeking offspring should diligently give the middle one preceded by mantras. / Seeking supreme beauty, he constantly gives it to cows;

2.12.s:
prajñāṃ caiva yaśaḥ kīrttimapsu vai saṃprayacchati /
prārthayandīrghāmāyuśca vāyasebhyaḥ prayacchati //
2.12.d:
प्रज्ञां चैव यशः कीर्त्तिमप्सु वै संप्रयच्छति ।
प्रार्थयन्दीर्घामायुश्च वायसेभ्यः प्रयच्छति ॥
2.12.m: he gives it into the waters [seeking] wisdom, renown, and fame; / praying for a long lifespan, he gives it to crows;

2.12.s:
sokumāryamathānvicchankukkuṭebhyaḥ prayacchati /
evametatsamuddiṣṭaṃ piṇḍanirvapaṇe phalam //
2.12.d:
सोकुमार्यमथान्विच्छन्कुक्कुटेभ्यः प्रयच्छति ।
एवमेतत्समुद्दिष्टं पिण्डनिर्वपणे फलम् ॥
2.12.m: and desiring tenderness of youth, he gives it to cocks. / In this way, this fruit has been declared regarding the offering of the food ball.

2.12.s:
ākāśe gamayedvāpi apsu vā dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ /
pitṝṇāṃ sthānamākāśaṃ dakṣiṇā caiva digbhevet //
2.12.d:
आकाशे गमयेद्वापि अप्सु वा दक्षिणामुखः ।
पितॄणां स्थानमाकाशं दक्षिणा चैव दिग्भेवेत् ॥
2.12.m: Or facing south, he should cast it into the air or into the waters; / for the place of the ancestors is the air and the southern direction.

2.12.s:
eke viprāḥ punaḥ prāhuḥ piṇḍoddharaṇamagrataḥ /
anujñātastu tairvipraiḥ kāmasuddhriyatāmit //
2.12.d:
एके विप्राः पुनः प्राहुः पिण्डोद्धरणमग्रतः ।
अनुज्ञातस्तु तैर्विप्रैः कामसुद्ध्रियतामित् ॥
2.12.m: Other brāhmaṇas, however, say that the raising of the food ball [is done] in front; / and permitted by those brāhmaṇas with the words, ‘Let it be raised at will,’

2.12.s:
puṣpāṇāṃ ca phalānāṃ ca bhakṣyāṇāmannatastathā /
agramuddhṛtya sarveṣāṃ juhuyāddhavyavāhane //
2.12.d:
पुष्पाणां च फलानां च भक्ष्याणामन्नतस्तथा ।
अग्रमुद्धृत्य सर्वेषां जुहुयाद्धव्यवाहने ॥
2.12.m: having taken the choice portion from all the flowers, fruits, and edible foods, / he should offer it into the fire-bearer [Agni].

2.12.s:
bhaṅyamannaṃ tathā peyaṃ mūlāni ca phalāni ca /
hutvāgnau ca tataḥ piṇḍānnirvapeddakṣiṇā mukhaḥ //
2.12.d:
भङ्यमन्नं तथा पेयं मूलानि च फलानि च ।
हुत्वाग्नौ च ततः पिण्डान्निर्वपेद्दक्षिणा मुखः ॥
2.12.m: Having offered into the fire edible food, drink, roots, and fruits, / he should then, facing south, offer the food balls.

2.12.s:
vaivasvatāya somāya hutvā piṇḍānnivedya ca /
udakānnayanaṃ kṛtvā paścādviprāṃśca bhojayet //
2.12.d:
वैवस्वताय सोमाय हुत्वा पिण्डान्निवेद्य च ।
उदकान्नयनं कृत्वा पश्चाद्विप्रांश्च भोजयेत् ॥
2.12.m: Having offered to Vaivasvata and to Soma, and having presented the food balls, / and having carried out the rinsing with water, he should feed the brāhmaṇas afterwards.

2.12.s:
anupūrvaṃ tato viprānbhakṣyairannaiśca śaktitaḥ /
snigdhairuṣṇaiḥ sugandhaiśca tarpayettānrasairapi //
2.12.d:
अनुपूर्वं ततो विप्रान्भक्ष्यैरन्नैश्च शक्तितः ।
स्निग्धैरुष्णैः सुगन्धैश्च तर्पयेत्तान्रसैरपि ॥
2.12.m: Then, according to order and to his ability, with foods and edibles / that are unctuous, hot, and fragrant, and with savory liquids, he should gratify those brāhmaṇas.

2.12.s:
ekāgraḥ paryupāsīnaḥ prayataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitaḥ /
tatparaḥ śraddadhānaśca kāmānāpnoti mānavaḥ //
2.12.d:
एकाग्रः पर्युपासीनः प्रयतः प्राञ्जलिः स्थितः ।
तत्परः श्रद्दधानश्च कामानाप्नोति मानवः ॥
2.12.m: Attentive, sitting nearby, restrained, standing with folded hands, / devoted to them and full of faith, a man attains his desires.

2.12.s:
akṣudratvaṃ kṛtajñatvaṃ dākṣiṇyaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ vacaḥ /
tapo yajñāṃśca dānaṃ ca prayacchanti pitāmahāḥ //
2.12.d:
अक्षुद्रत्वं कृतज्ञत्वं दाक्षिण्यं संस्कृतं वचः ।
तपो यज्ञांश्च दानं च प्रयच्छन्ति पितामहाः ॥
2.12.m: Freedom from meanness, gratitude, courtesy, refined speech, / ascetic practice, sacrifices, and charity—the grandfathers bestow [all these].

2.12.s:
ataḥ paraṃ vidhiṃ saumyaṃ bhuktavatsu dvijātiṣu /
ānupūrvyeṇa vihitaṃ tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu //
2.12.d:
अतः परं विधिं सौम्यं भुक्तवत्सु द्विजातिषु ।
आनुपूर्व्येण विहितं तन्मे निगदतः शृणु ॥
2.12.m: After this, hear from me as I proclaim the gentle rule laid down in order / when the twice-born have finished eating.

2.12.s:
prokṣya bhūmimathoddhṛtya pūrvaṃ pitṛparāyaṇaḥ /
tato 'nnivikiraṃ kuryādvidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā //
2.12.d:
प्रोक्ष्य भूमिमथोद्धृत्य पूर्वं पितृपरायणः ।
ततो ऽन्निविकिरं कुर्याद्विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा ॥
2.12.m: Having sprinkled the ground and previously swept it, devoted to the ancestors, / he should then scatter the food according to the rite observed in the rules.

2.12.s:
svadhā vācya tato viprān vidhivadbhūritakṣiṇān /
annaśeṣamanujñāpya satkṛtya dvijasattamān //
2.12.d:
स्वधा वाच्य ततो विप्रान् विधिवद्भूरितक्षिणान् ।
अन्नशेषमनुज्ञाप्य सत्कृत्य द्विजसत्तमान् ॥
2.12.m: Having recited ‘svadhā’, and having honored the excellent twice-born with abundant sacrificial gifts according to rule, / having asked permission concerning the remnant of the food,

2.12.s:
prāñjaliḥ prayataścaiva anugamya visarjayet //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīye
upoddhātapāde śrāddhakalpe dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ // 12//
2.12.d:
प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतश्चैव अनुगम्य विसर्जयेत् ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीये
उपोद्धातपादे श्राद्धकल्पे द्वादशो ऽध्यायः ॥ 12॥
2.12.m:
with folded hands and self-restrained, he should accompany them and dismiss them.

Thus ends the twelfth chapter on the rules of śrāddha in the Upoddhātapāda, the third middle section, of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa spoken by Vāyu. // 12

2.13.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
sakṛdabhyarcitāḥ prītā bhavanti pitaro 'vyayāḥ /
yogātmāno mahātmāno vipāpmāno mahaujasaḥ //
2.13.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
सकृदभ्यर्चिताः प्रीता भवन्ति पितरो ऽव्ययाः ।
योगात्मानो महात्मानो विपाप्मानो महौजसः ॥
2.13.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Worshipped but once, the imperishable ancestors are pleased— / those great souls consisting of yoga, free from sin, possessing great splendor.

2.13.s:
pretya ca svargalokāya kāmaiśca bahulaṃ bhuvi /
yeṣu vāpyanugṛhṇanti mokṣaprāptiḥ krameṇa tu //
2.13.d:
प्रेत्य च स्वर्गलोकाय कामैश्च बहुलं भुवि ।
येषु वाप्यनुगृह्णन्ति मोक्षप्राप्तिः क्रमेण तु ॥
2.13.m: And after dying, [they go] to the heavenly world; and with abundant desires on earth, / or upon whom they bestow grace, there is attainment of liberation in due course.

2.13.s:
tāni vakṣyāmyahaṃ saumya sarāṃsi saritastathā /
tīrthāni caiva puṇyāni deśāṃśchailāṃstathāśramān //
2.13.d:
तानि वक्ष्याम्यहं सौम्य सरांसि सरितस्तथा ।
तीर्थानि चैव पुण्यानि देशांश्छैलांस्तथाश्रमान् ॥
2.13.m: I shall tell of them, gentle one—the lakes as well as the rivers, / the holy tīrthas, regions, mountains, and hermitages.

2.13.s:
puṇyo hi triṣu lokeṣu sadaivāmarakaṇṭakaḥ /
parvatapravaraḥ puṇyaḥ siddhayāraṇasevitaḥ //
2.13.d:
पुण्यो हि त्रिषु लोकेषु सदैवामरकण्टकः ।
पर्वतप्रवरः पुण्यः सिद्धयारणसेवितः ॥
2.13.m: Amarkaṇṭaka is indeed holy in the three worlds at all times, / an eminent and holy mountain visited by Siddhas and Cāraṇas,

2.13.s:
yatra varṣasahasrāṇi prayutānyarbudāni ca /
tapaḥ suduścaraṃ tepe bhagavānaṅgirāḥ purā //
2.13.d:
यत्र वर्षसहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च ।
तपः सुदुश्चरं तेपे भगवानङ्गिराः पुरा ॥
2.13.m: where the blessed Aṅgiras of old performed austerity very hard to practice / for thousands, hundreds of thousands, and hundreds of millions of years;

2.13.s:
yatra mṛtyorgatirnnāsti tathaivāsurarakṣasām /
na bhayaṃ naiva cālakṣmīryāvadbhūmirddhariṣyati //
2.13.d:
यत्र मृत्योर्गतिर्न्नास्ति तथैवासुररक्षसाम् ।
न भयं नैव चालक्ष्मीर्यावद्भूमिर्द्धरिष्यति ॥
2.13.m: where death has no access, nor do asuras and rākṣasas; / there is neither fear nor misfortune as long as the earth endures.

2.13.s:
tapasā tejasā tasya bhrajate sa nagottamaḥ /
śṛṅge mālyavato nityaṃ vahniḥ saṃvarttako yathā //
2.13.d:
तपसा तेजसा तस्य भ्रजते स नगोत्तमः ।
शृङ्गे माल्यवतो नित्यं वह्निः संवर्त्तको यथा ॥
2.13.m: By his austerity and splendor, that best of mountains shines / like the fire of dissolution constantly on the peak of Mālyavat.

2.13.s:
mṛdavastu sugandhāśca hemābhāḥ priyadarśanāḥ /
śāntāḥkuśā iti khyātāḥ paridakṣiṇanarmadām //
2.13.d:
मृदवस्तु सुगन्धाश्च हेमाभाः प्रियदर्शनाः ।
शान्ताःकुशा इति ख्याताः परिदक्षिणनर्मदाम् ॥
2.13.m: The kuśa grasses known to be soft, fragrant, golden-hued, pleasant to behold, / and tranquil surround the Narmadā to the right.

2.13.s:
dṛṣṭavānsvargasopānaṃ bhagavānaṅgirāḥ purā /
agnihotre mahātejāḥ prastārārthaṃ kuśottamān //
2.13.d:
दृष्टवान्स्वर्गसोपानं भगवानङ्गिराः पुरा ।
अग्निहोत्रे महातेजाः प्रस्तारार्थं कुशोत्तमान् ॥
2.13.m: The blessed Aṅgiras of great splendor formerly saw [them as] a stairway to heaven, / [being] the best kuśa grasses for the sacrificial seat in the agnihotra.

2.13.s:
teṣu darbheṣu yaḥ piṇḍānmarakaṇṭaṭakaparvate /
dadyātsakṛdapi prājñastasya vakṣyāmi yatphalam //
2.13.d:
तेषु दर्भेषु यः पिण्डान्मरकण्टटकपर्वते ।
दद्यात्सकृदपि प्राज्ञस्तस्य वक्ष्यामि यत्फलम् ॥
2.13.m: The wise man who offers food balls upon those darbha grasses on Mount Amarakaṇṭaka / even once—I shall tell of his fruit:

2.13.s:
tadbhavatyakṣayaṃ śrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāṃ prītivardhanam /
antarddhānaṃ ca gacchanti kṣetramāsādya tatsadā //
2.13.d:
तद्भवत्यक्षयं श्राद्धं पितॄणां प्रीतिवर्धनम् ।
अन्तर्द्धानं च गच्छन्ति क्षेत्रमासाद्य तत्सदा ॥
2.13.m: That śrāddha becomes imperishable, increasing the delight of the ancestors; / and having reached that sacred place, they always attain invisibility.

2.13.s:
tatra jvālāsaraḥ puṇyaṃ dṛśyate cāpi parvasu /
saśalyānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ viśalyakaraṇī nadī //
2.13.d:
तत्र ज्वालासरः पुण्यं दृश्यते चापि पर्वसु ।
सशल्यानां च सत्त्वानां विशल्यकरणी नदी ॥
2.13.m: The holy Jvālāsaras is seen there on conjunction days, / and the river that removes arrow-heads from living beings with darts [in them],

2.13.s:
prāgdakṣiṇāyatāvarttā vāpī sā sunagottame /
kaliṅgadeśapaścārddhe śṛṅge mālyavato vibhoḥ //
2.13.d:
प्राग्दक्षिणायतावर्त्ता वापी सा सुनगोत्तमे ।
कलिङ्गदेशपश्चार्द्धे शृङ्गे माल्यवतो विभोः ॥
2.13.m: that pool having an eddy extending towards the southeast on that excellent mountain / on the western half of the Kaliṅga country, on the peak of Mālyavat of the lord.

2.13.s:
siddhikṣetramṛṣiśreṣṭhā yaduktaṃ paramaṃ bhuvi /
saṃmataṃ devadaityānāṃ ślokaṃ cāpyuśanā jagau //
2.13.d:
सिद्धिक्षेत्रमृषिश्रेष्ठा यदुक्तं परमं भुवि ।
संमतं देवदैत्यानां श्लोकं चाप्युशना जगौ ॥
2.13.m: O best of ṛṣis, it is declared the supreme field of accomplishment on earth, / agreed upon by gods and daityas; and Uśanas sang a verse [about it]:

2.13.s:
dhanyāste puruṣā loke ye prāpyāmarakaṇṭakam /
pitṝnsaṃtarpayiṣyantiśrāddhe pitṛparāyaṇāḥ //
2.13.d:
धन्यास्ते पुरुषा लोके ये प्राप्यामरकण्टकम् ।
पितॄन्संतर्पयिष्यन्तिश्राद्धे पितृपरायणाः ॥
2.13.m: ‘Blessed are those men in the world who, having reached Amarakaṇṭaka, / satisfy their ancestors in a śrāddha, wholly devoted to their ancestors.

2.13.s:
alpena tapasā siddhiṃ gamiṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ /
sakṛdevārcitāstatra svargamāmarakaṇṭake //
2.13.d:
अल्पेन तपसा सिद्धिं गमिष्यन्ति न संशयः ।
सकृदेवार्चितास्तत्र स्वर्गमामरकण्टके ॥
2.13.m: By little austerity, they will attain perfection, there is no doubt; / worshipped but once there at Amarakaṇṭaka, [the ancestors go to] heaven.’

2.13.s:
mahendraḥparvataḥ puṇyo ramyaḥ śakraniṣevitaḥ /
tatrāruhya bhavetpūtaḥ śrāddhaṃ caiva mahāphalam //
2.13.d:
महेन्द्रःपर्वतः पुण्यो रम्यः शक्रनिषेवितः ।
तत्रारुह्य भवेत्पूतः श्राद्धं चैव महाफलम् ॥
2.13.m: Mount Mahendra is holy, delightful, and resorted to by Śakra; / having climbed it, one becomes purified, and a śrāddha [performed there] bears great fruit.

2.13.s:
vailāṭaśikhare yuktvā divyaṃ cakṣuḥ pravartate /
adhṛṣyaścaiva bhūtānāṃ devavaccarate mahīm //
2.13.d:
वैलाटशिखरे युक्त्वा दिव्यं चक्षुः प्रवर्तते ।
अधृष्यश्चैव भूतानां देववच्चरते महीम् ॥
2.13.m: Engaging in yoga on the summit of Vailāṭa, divine vision arises; / unassailable by living beings, he wanders the earth like a god.

2.13.s:
saptagodāvare caiva gokarṇe ca tapovane /
aśvamedhaphalaṃ snātvā tatra dattvā bhavettataḥ //
2.13.d:
सप्तगोदावरे चैव गोकर्णे च तपोवने ।
अश्वमेधफलं स्नात्वा तत्र दत्त्वा भवेत्ततः ॥
2.13.m: At Saptagodāvara and in the hermitage at Gokarṇa, / having bathed and given [gifts] there, the fruit of an aśvamedha arises from that.

2.13.s:
dhūtapāpasthalaṃ prāpya pūtaḥ snātvā bhavennaraḥ /
rudrastatra tapastepe devadevo maheśvaraḥ //
2.13.d:
धूतपापस्थलं प्राप्य पूतः स्नात्वा भवेन्नरः ।
रुद्रस्तत्र तपस्तेपे देवदेवो महेश्वरः ॥
2.13.m: Having reached the place called Dhūtapāpa, a man, having bathed, becomes purified; / Rudra, the god of gods, Maheśvara, performed austerities there.

2.13.s:
gokarṇe nihitaṃ devair nāstikānāṃ nidarśanam /
abrāhmaṇasya sāvitrīṃ paṭhatastu praṇaśyati //
2.13.d:
गोकर्णे निहितं देवैर् नास्तिकानां निदर्शनम् ।
अब्राह्मणस्य सावित्रीं पठतस्तु प्रणश्यति ॥
2.13.m: At Gokarṇa an example for non-believers was set by the gods: / for a non-brāhmaṇa reciting the Sāvitrī, it perishes.

2.13.s:
devarṣibhavane śṛṅge siddhacāraṇasevite /
āruhyataṃ niya mavāṃstato yāti triviṣṭapam //
2.13.d:
देवर्षिभवने शृङ्गे सिद्धचारणसेविते ।
आरुह्यतं निय मवांस्ततो याति त्रिविष्टपम् ॥
2.13.m:
Ascending that peak, the dwelling of divine seers, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas,
one who is self-restrained goes from there to heaven.

2.13.s:
divyaiścandanavṛkṣaiśca pādapairupaśobhitam /
āpaścandanasaṃyuktāḥ spandeti satataṃ tataḥ //
2.13.d:
दिव्यैश्चन्दनवृक्षैश्च पादपैरुपशोभितम् ।
आपश्चन्दनसंयुक्ताः स्पन्देति सततं ततः ॥
2.13.m:
Adorned with heavenly sandalwood trees and various plants,
waters mixed with sandalwood flow constantly from there.

2.13.s:
nadī pravartate tābhyastāmraparṇīti nāmataḥ /
yā candanamahākhaṇḍāddakṣiṇaṃ yāti sāgaram //
2.13.d:
नदी प्रवर्तते ताभ्यस्ताम्रपर्णीति नामतः ।
या चन्दनमहाखण्डाद्दक्षिणं याति सागरम् ॥
2.13.m:
From those [waters] issues a river named Tāmraparṇī,
which flows from the great sandalwood grove to the southern sea.

2.13.s:
nadyāstasyāśca tāmrāyāstūhyamānā mahodadhau /
śaṅkhā bhavanti śuktyaśca jāyate yāsu mauktikam //
2.13.d:
नद्यास्तस्याश्च ताम्रायास्तूह्यमाना महोदधौ ।
शङ्खा भवन्ति शुक्त्यश्च जायते यासु मौक्तिकम् ॥
2.13.m:
Borne by that river Tāmrā into the great ocean,
there are conches and oysters within which pearls are born.

2.13.s:
udakānayanaṃ kṛtvā śaṅkhamauktikasaṃyutam /
ādhibhirvyādhibhiścaiva muktā yāntyamarāvatīm //
2.13.d:
उदकानयनं कृत्वा शङ्खमौक्तिकसंयुतम् ।
आधिभिर्व्याधिभिश्चैव मुक्ता यान्त्यमरावतीम् ॥
2.13.m:
Having offered water accompanied by conches and pearls,
freed from mental agonies and physical diseases, they go to Amarāvatī.

2.13.s:
candanebhyaḥ prasūtānāṃ śaṅkhānāṃ mauktikasya vā /
pāpakarttṝnapi pitṝṃstārayanti yathāśruti //
2.13.d:
चन्दनेभ्यः प्रसूतानां शङ्खानां मौक्तिकस्य वा ।
पापकर्त्तॄनपि पितॄंस्तारयन्ति यथाश्रुति ॥
2.13.m:
[By means] of the conches or the pearls produced from the sandalwood [grove],
they deliver even fathers who have committed sins, according to the sacred tradition.

2.13.s:
candratīrthe kumāryāṃ ca kāverīprabhave kṣaye /
śrīparvatasya tīrtheṣu vaikṛte ca tathā girau //
2.13.d:
चन्द्रतीर्थे कुमार्यां च कावेरीप्रभवे क्षये ।
श्रीपर्वतस्य तीर्थेषु वैकृते च तथा गिरौ ॥
2.13.m:
At Candratīrtha and Kumārī, at the source of the Kāverī, at Kṣaya,
at the holy sites of Śrīparvata and on the mountain Vaikṛta,

2.13.s:
ekasthā yatra dṛśyante vṛkṣāhyauśīraparvate /
palāśāḥ khadirā bilvāḥ plakṣāśvatthavikaṅkatāḥ //
2.13.d:
एकस्था यत्र दृश्यन्ते वृक्षाह्यौशीरपर्वते ।
पलाशाः खदिरा बिल्वाः प्लक्षाश्वत्थविकङ्कताः ॥
2.13.m:
where trees are seen standing together on the Auśīra mountain—
palāśas, khadiras, bilvas, plakṣas, aśvatthas, and vikaṅkatas—

2.13.s:
evaṃ dvimaṇḍalāviddhaṃ vijñeyaṃ dvijasattamāḥ /
asmiṃstyaktvā janoṃ'gāti kṣipraṃ yātyamarāvatīm //
2.13.d:
एवं द्विमण्डलाविद्धं विज्ञेयं द्विजसत्तमाः ।
अस्मिंस्त्यक्त्वा जनोंऽगाति क्षिप्रं यात्यमरावतीम् ॥
2.13.m:
thus should it be known as encompassed by two circles, O best of the twice-born;
leaving one's body here, a person goes swiftly to Amarāvatī.

2.13.s:
śrīparvatasya tīrthe tu vaikṛte ca tathā girau /
karmāṇi tu prayuktā ni siddhyanti prabhavāpyaye //
2.13.d:
श्रीपर्वतस्य तीर्थे तु वैकृते च तथा गिरौ ।
कर्माणि तु प्रयुक्ता नि सिद्ध्यन्ति प्रभवाप्यये ॥
2.13.m:
At the holy site of Śrīparvata and likewise on mount Vaikṛta,
rituals performed at the origin and destruction [of the world] succeed.

2.13.s:
duṣprayuktā hi pitṛṣu suprayogā bhavantyuta /
pitṝṇāṃ duhitā puṇyā narmadā saritāṃ varā //
2.13.d:
दुष्प्रयुक्ता हि पितृषु सुप्रयोगा भवन्त्युत ।
पितॄणां दुहिता पुण्या नर्मदा सरितां वरा ॥
2.13.m:
Indeed, even ill-performed [offerings] to the ancestors become well-performed;
moreover, the sacred Narmadā, daughter of the ancestors, is the best of rivers,

2.13.s:
yatra śrāddhāni dattāṃni hyakṣayāṇi bhavantyuta /
māṭharasya vane puṇye siddhacāraṇasevite //
2.13.d:
यत्र श्राद्धानि दत्तांनि ह्यक्षयाणि भवन्त्युत ।
माठरस्य वने पुण्ये सिद्धचारणसेविते ॥
2.13.m:
where indeed śrāddhas that are offered become imperishable,
in the holy forest of Māṭhara, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

2.13.s:
antarddhānena gacchanti yuktvā tasminmahā girau /
vindhye caiva girau puṇye dharmādharmanidarśanīm //
2.13.d:
अन्तर्द्धानेन गच्छन्ति युक्त्वा तस्मिन्महा गिरौ ।
विन्ध्ये चैव गिरौ पुण्ये धर्माधर्मनिदर्शनीम् ॥
2.13.m:
Fixing [their minds] on that great mountain, they depart by becoming invisible;
and on the holy Vindhya mountain, [there is a stream] revealing dharma and adharma,

2.13.s:
dhārāṃ pāpā na paśyanti dhārāṃ paśyanti sādhavaḥ /
tatra taddṛśyate pāpaṃ keṣāṃ citpāpakarmaṇām //
2.13.d:
धारां पापा न पश्यन्ति धारां पश्यन्ति साधवः ।
तत्र तद्दृश्यते पापं केषां चित्पापकर्मणाम् ॥
2.13.m:
a stream which the wicked do not see, [but] the virtuous do see;
there that sin of certain evildoers becomes visible.

2.13.s:
kailāse yā mataṅgasya vāpī pāpaniṣūdanī /
snātvā tasyā divaṃ yānti kāmacārā vihaṅgamāḥ //
2.13.d:
कैलासे या मतङ्गस्य वापी पापनिषूदनी ।
स्नात्वा तस्या दिवं यान्ति कामचारा विहङ्गमाः ॥
2.13.m:
The pool of Mataṅga on Kailāsa destroys sin;
having bathed in it, birds that move at will go to heaven.

2.13.s:
śaurpārake tathā tīrthe parvate pālamañjare /
pāṇḍukūpe samudrānte piṇḍārakataṭe tathā //
2.13.d:
शौर्पारके तथा तीर्थे पर्वते पालमञ्जरे ।
पाण्डुकूपे समुद्रान्ते पिण्डारकतटे तथा ॥
2.13.m:
Likewise at the holy site in Śūrpāraka, on Mount Pālamañjara,
at Pāṇḍukūpa on the edge of the sea, and on the shore of Piṇḍāraka,

2.13.s:
vimale ca vipāpe ca saṃkalpaṃ prāpya cākṣayam /
śrīvṛkṣe citrakūṭe ca jaṃbūmārge ca nityaśaḥ //
2.13.d:
विमले च विपापे च संकल्पं प्राप्य चाक्षयम् ।
श्रीवृक्षे चित्रकूटे च जंबूमार्गे च नित्यशः ॥
2.13.m:
and at Vimala and Vipāpa, attaining an imperishable resolve,
at Śrīvṛkṣa, Citrakūṭa, and constantly at Jaṃbūmārga,

2.13.s:
asitasya girau puṇye yogācāryasya dhīmataḥ /
tatrāpi śrāddhamānantyamasitāyāṃ ca nityaśaḥ //
2.13.d:
असितस्य गिरौ पुण्ये योगाचार्यस्य धीमतः ।
तत्रापि श्राद्धमानन्त्यमसितायां च नित्यशः ॥
2.13.m:
on the holy mountain of the wise yoga master Asita—
there too a śrāddha [brings] endless [fruits], and constantly at the Asitā river.

2.13.s:
puṣkareṣvakṣayaṃ śrāddhaṃ tapaścaiva mahāphalamā /
mahodadhau prabhāse ca tadvadeva vinirdiśet //
2.13.d:
पुष्करेष्वक्षयं श्राद्धं तपश्चैव महाफलमा ।
महोदधौ प्रभासे च तद्वदेव विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
2.13.m:
At Puṣkara a śrāddha is imperishable, and austerity bears great fruit;
one should declare the very same regarding the great ocean and Prabhāsa.

2.13.s:
devikāyāṃ vṛṣo nāma kūpaḥ siddhaniṣevitaḥ /
samutpatanti tasyāpo gavāṃ śabdena nityaśaḥ //
2.13.d:
देविकायां वृषो नाम कूपः सिद्धनिषेवितः ।
समुत्पतन्ति तस्यापो गवां शब्देन नित्यशः ॥
2.13.m:
On the Devikā [river] there is a well named Vṛṣa frequented by Siddhas;
its waters constantly surge up at the bellowing of cows.

2.13.s:
yogeśvaraiḥ sadā juṣṭaḥ sarvapāpabahiṣkṛtaḥ /
dadyācchrāddhaṃ tu yastasmiṃstasya vakṣyāmi yatphalam //
2.13.d:
योगेश्वरैः सदा जुष्टः सर्वपापबहिष्कृतः ।
दद्याच्छ्राद्धं तु यस्तस्मिंस्तस्य वक्ष्यामि यत्फलम् ॥
2.13.m:
Always visited by lords of yoga, it is free from all sins;
whoever offers a śrāddha there, I shall describe the fruit for him.

2.13.s:
akṣayaṃ sarvakāmīyaṃ śrāddhaṃ prīṇāti vai pitṝn /
jātavedaḥ śilā tatra sākṣādagneḥ sanātanāt //
2.13.d:
अक्षयं सर्वकामीयं श्राद्धं प्रीणाति वै पितॄन् ।
जातवेदः शिला तत्र साक्षादग्नेः सनातनात् ॥
2.13.m:
An imperishable śrāddha fulfilling all desires truly pleases the ancestors;
there is the stone of Jātavedas, [manifested] directly from the eternal Fire.

2.13.s:
śrāddhāni cāgnikāryaṃ ca tatra kuryātsadā kṣayam /
yastvagniṃ praviśettatra nākapṛṣṭhe sa modate //
2.13.d:
श्राद्धानि चाग्निकार्यं च तत्र कुर्यात्सदा क्षयम् ।
यस्त्वग्निं प्रविशेत्तत्र नाकपृष्ठे स मोदते ॥
2.13.m:
One should always perform śrāddhas and rituals to fire there at the time of the waning moon;
and he who enters the fire there rejoices in the highest heaven.

2.13.s:
agniśāntaḥ punarjātastatra dattaṃ tato 'kṣayam /
daśāśvamedhike tīrthe tīrthe pañcāśvamedhike //
2.13.d:
अग्निशान्तः पुनर्जातस्तत्र दत्तं ततो ऽक्षयम् ।
दशाश्वमेधिके तीर्थे तीर्थे पञ्चाश्वमेधिके ॥
2.13.m:
When the fire is extinguished, he is reborn; what is given there is therefore imperishable.
At the holy site Daśāśvamedhika and at the holy site Pañcāśvamedhika,

2.13.s:
yathoddiṣṭaphalaṃ teṣāṃ kratūnāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ /
khyātaṃ hayaśiro nāma tīrthaṃ sadyo varapradam //
2.13.d:
यथोद्दिष्टफलं तेषां क्रतूनां नात्र संशयः ।
ख्यातं हयशिरो नाम तीर्थं सद्यो वरप्रदम् ॥
2.13.m:
the fruit of those sacrifices is as prescribed, there is no doubt of this;
the well-known holy site named Hayaśiras immediately grants boons.

2.13.s:
śrāddhaṃ tatra sadākṣayyaṃ dātā svarge ca modate /
śrāddhaṃ suṃdanisuṃde ca deyaṃ pāpaniṣū danam //
2.13.d:
श्राद्धं तत्र सदाक्षय्यं दाता स्वर्गे च मोदते ।
श्राद्धं सुंदनिसुंदे च देयं पापनिषू दनम् ॥
2.13.m:
A śrāddha there is always imperishable, and the giver rejoices in heaven;
a śrāddha should be offered at Sundanīsunda, destroying sins.

2.13.s:
śrāddhaṃ tatrākṣayaṃ proktaṃ japahomatapāṃsi ca /
jatuṅge śubhe tīrthe tarpayetsatataṃ pitṝn //
2.13.d:
श्राद्धं तत्राक्षयं प्रोक्तं जपहोमतपांसि च ।
जतुङ्गे शुभे तीर्थे तर्पयेत्सततं पितॄन् ॥
2.13.m:
A śrāddha there is declared imperishable, as are recitation, oblation, and austerities;
at the auspicious holy site Jatuṅga one should continually gratify the ancestors.

2.13.s:
dṛśyate parvasu cchāyā yatra nityaṃ divaukasām /
pṛthivyāmakṣayaṃ dattaṃ virajā yatra pādapaḥ //
2.13.d:
दृश्यते पर्वसु च्छाया यत्र नित्यं दिवौकसाम् ।
पृथिव्यामक्षयं दत्तं विरजा यत्र पादपः ॥
2.13.m:
Where the shadow of the gods is always visible on the sacred days,
what is given on earth where the Virajā tree [stands] is imperishable.

2.13.s:
yogeśvaraiḥ sadā juṣṭaḥ sarvapāpabahiṣkṛtaḥ /
dadyācchrāddhaṃ tu yastasmiṃstasya vakṣyāmi yatphalam //
2.13.d:
योगेश्वरैः सदा जुष्टः सर्वपापबहिष्कृतः ।
दद्याच्छ्राद्धं तु यस्तस्मिंस्तस्य वक्ष्यामि यत्फलम् ॥
2.13.m:
Always visited by lords of yoga, it is free from all sins;
whoever offers a śrāddha there, I shall describe the fruit for him:

2.13.s:
arcitāstena vai sākṣādbhavanti pitaraḥ sadā /
asmiṃlloke vaśī ca syātpretya svarge mahī yate //
2.13.d:
अर्चितास्तेन वै साक्षाद्भवन्ति पितरः सदा ।
अस्मिंल्लोके वशी च स्यात्प्रेत्य स्वर्गे मही यते ॥
2.13.m:
by him the ancestors are indeed worshipped directly at all times;
he would become a master in this world, and after dying, he is honored in heaven.

2.13.s:
prāyaśo madravā puṇyā śivo nāma hradastathā /
tatra vyāsasaraḥ puṇyaṃ divyo brahmahradastathā //
2.13.d:
प्रायशो मद्रवा पुण्या शिवो नाम ह्रदस्तथा ।
तत्र व्याससरः पुण्यं दिव्यो ब्रह्मह्रदस्तथा ॥
2.13.m:
For the most part, the Madravā is holy, and likewise the pool named Śiva;
there is the holy lake of Vyāsa and the divine Brahmahrada,

2.13.s:
ūrjjantaḥ parvataḥ puṇyo yatra yogeśvarālayaḥ /
atraiva cāśramaḥ puṇyo vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ //
2.13.d:
ऊर्ज्जन्तः पर्वतः पुण्यो यत्र योगेश्वरालयः ।
अत्रैव चाश्रमः पुण्यो वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः ॥
2.13.m:
and the holy mountain Ūrjjanta, where the abode of the lords of yoga is;
and right here is the holy hermitage of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha.

2.13.s:
ṛgyajuḥ sāmaśirasaḥ kapotāḥ puṣpasāhvayāḥ /
ākhyāna pañcamā vedāḥ sṛṣṭā hyete svayaṃbhuvā //
2.13.d:
ऋग्यजुः सामशिरसः कपोताः पुष्पसाह्वयाः ।
आख्यान पञ्चमा वेदाः सृष्टा ह्येते स्वयंभुवा ॥
2.13.m:
Those named Kapota and Puṣpa, headed by the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma,
and the Vedas with the histories as the fifth, were created by Svayambhū.

2.13.s:
gatvaitānmucyate pāpaddvijo vahniṃ samāśrayan /
śrāddhaṃ cānantyameteṣu japahomatapāṃsi ca //
2.13.d:
गत्वैतान्मुच्यते पापद्द्विजो वह्निं समाश्रयन् ।
श्राद्धं चानन्त्यमेतेषु जपहोमतपांसि च ॥
2.13.m:
Going to these, a twice-born, taking refuge in the fire, is freed from sin;
and a śrāddha performed at these, as well as recitation, oblations, and austerities, brings endless [reward].

2.13.s:
puṇḍarīke mahātīrthe puṇḍarīkasamaṃ phalam /
brahmatīrthe mahāprājña sarvayajñasamaṃ phalam //
2.13.d:
पुण्डरीके महातीर्थे पुण्डरीकसमं फलम् ।
ब्रह्मतीर्थे महाप्राज्ञ सर्वयज्ञसमं फलम् ॥
2.13.m:
At the great holy site Puṇḍarīka, the fruit equals [that of] a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice;
at Brahmatīrtha, O very wise one, the fruit equals [that of] all sacrifices.

2.13.s:
siṃdhusāgarasaṃbhede tathā pañcanade kṣayam /
virajāyāṃ tathā puṇyaṃ madravāyāṃ ca parvate //
2.13.d:
सिंधुसागरसंभेदे तथा पञ्चनदे क्षयम् ।
विरजायां तथा पुण्यं मद्रवायां च पर्वते ॥
2.13.m:
At the confluence of the Sindhu and the ocean, and likewise at Pañcanada on the new moon,
and on the holy Virajā, and on Mount Madravā,

2.13.s:
deyaṃ saptanade śrāddhaṃ mānase vā viśeṣataḥ /
mahākūṭe hyanante ca girau trikakude tathā //
2.13.d:
देयं सप्तनदे श्राद्धं मानसे वा विशेषतः ।
महाकूटे ह्यनन्ते च गिरौ त्रिककुदे तथा ॥
2.13.m:
a śrāddha should be offered at Saptanada, or especially at Mānasa,
on Mahākūṭa, on Ananta, and likewise on Mount Trikakud.

2.13.s:
saṃdhyāyāṃ ca mahānadyāṃ dṛśyate mahādadbhutam /
aśraddadhānaṃ nābhyeti sā cābhyeti dhṛtavratam //
2.13.d:
संध्यायां च महानद्यां दृश्यते महादद्भुतम् ।
अश्रद्दधानं नाभ्येति सा चाभ्येति धृतव्रतम् ॥
2.13.m:
At twilight on the great river, a great wonder is seen:
it does not approach one who lacks faith, but it approaches one who keeps his vows.

2.13.s:
saṃśrayitvaikamekena sāyāhnaṃ prati nityaśaḥ /
tasmindeyaṃ sadā śrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāmakṣayārthinām //
2.13.d:
संश्रयित्वैकमेकेन सायाह्नं प्रति नित्यशः ।
तस्मिन्देयं सदा श्राद्धं पितॄणामक्षयार्थिनाम् ॥
2.13.m:
Approaching one by one constantly toward evening,
one should always offer a śrāddha there, desiring imperishability for the ancestors.

2.13.s:
kṛtātmā vākṛtātmā ca yatra vijñāyate naraḥ /
svargamārgapradaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ sadyo varapradam //
2.13.d:
कृतात्मा वाकृतात्मा च यत्र विज्ञायते नरः ।
स्वर्गमार्गप्रदं नाम तीर्थं सद्यो वरप्रदम् ॥
2.13.m:
Where a person is recognized as either cultivated in self or uncultivated in self,
that holy site named Svargamārgaprada immediately grants boons,

2.13.s:
cīrāṇyutsṛjya yasmiṃstu divaṃ saptarṣayo gātāḥ /
adyāpi tāni dṛśyante cīrāṇyaṃbhogatāni tu //
2.13.d:
चीराण्युत्सृज्य यस्मिंस्तु दिवं सप्तर्षयो गाताः ।
अद्यापि तानि दृश्यन्ते चीराण्यंभोगतानि तु ॥
2.13.m:
where the seven seers, having cast off their bark garments, went to heaven;
even today those bark garments are seen submerged in the waters.

2.13.s:
snātvā svargamavāpnoti tasmiṃstīrthettame naraḥ /
khyātamāyatanaṃ tatra nandinaḥ siddhasevitam //
2.13.d:
स्नात्वा स्वर्गमवाप्नोति तस्मिंस्तीर्थेत्तमे नरः ।
ख्यातमायतनं तत्र नन्दिनः सिद्धसेवितम् ॥
2.13.m:
Having bathed at that best of holy sites, a man attains heaven;
there is the renowned sanctuary of Nandin, frequented by Siddhas.

2.13.s:
nandīśvarasya sā mūrttirnirācārairnadṛśyate /
dṛśyante kāñcanā yupāstvarciṣo bhāskarodaye //
2.13.d:
नन्दीश्वरस्य सा मूर्त्तिर्निराचारैर्नदृश्यते ।
दृश्यन्ते काञ्चना युपास्त्वर्चिषो भास्करोदये ॥
2.13.m:
That form of Nandīśvara is not seen by those lacking proper conduct;
golden sacrificial posts and rays of light are seen at sunrise.

2.13.s:
kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ tāṃstu gacchantyānanditā divam /
sarvataśca kurukṣetraṃ sutīrthaṃ tu viśeṣataḥ //
2.13.d:
कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं तांस्तु गच्छन्त्यानन्दिता दिवम् ।
सर्वतश्च कुरुक्षेत्रं सुतीर्थं तु विशेषतः ॥
2.13.m:
Having circumambulated them, they go to heaven rejoiced;
Kurukṣetra is good throughout, but especially as an excellent holy site.

2.13.s:
puṇyaṃ sanatkumārasya yogeśasya mahātmanaḥ /
kīrtyate ca tilāndattvā pitṛbhyovai sadākṣayam //
2.13.d:
पुण्यं सनत्कुमारस्य योगेशस्य महात्मनः ।
कीर्त्यते च तिलान्दत्त्वा पितृभ्योवै सदाक्षयम् ॥
2.13.m:
The holy [site] of the great-souled Sanatkumāra, the lord of yoga,
is renowned; offering sesame seeds to the ancestors there [is] truly ever imperishable.

2.13.s:
uktamevākṣayaṃ śrāddhaṃ dharmarājaniṣevitam /
śrāddhaṃ dattamamāvāsyāṃ vidhinā ca yathākramam //
2.13.d:
उक्तमेवाक्षयं श्राद्धं धर्मराजनिषेवितम् ।
श्राद्धं दत्तममावास्यां विधिना च यथाक्रमम् ॥
2.13.m:
An imperishable śrāddha frequented by the King of Dharma has been declared;
a śrāddha offered on the new-moon day in accordance with the rule and in due order,

2.13.s:
puṃsaḥ sannihitāyāṃ tu kurūkṣetre viśeṣataḥ /
arcayitvā pitṝṃstatra sa putrastvanṛṇo bhavet //
2.13.d:
पुंसः सन्निहितायां तु कुरूक्षेत्रे विशेषतः ।
अर्चयित्वा पितॄंस्तत्र स पुत्रस्त्वनृणो भवेत् ॥
2.13.m:
especially at the Sannihitā pool in Kurukṣetra,
by worshipping the ancestors there, that man, a son, becomes free from debt.

2.13.s:
sarasvatyāṃ vinaśane plakṣapraśravaṇe tathā /
vyāsatīrthe dṛṣadvatyāṃ triplakṣe ca viśeṣataḥ //
2.13.d:
सरस्वत्यां विनशने प्लक्षप्रश्रवणे तथा ।
व्यासतीर्थे दृषद्वत्यां त्रिप्लक्षे च विशेषतः ॥
2.13.m: On the Sarasvatī at Vinaśana, and likewise at Plakṣapraśravaṇa, / at Vyāsatīrtha, on the Dṛṣadvatī, and especially at Triplakṣa;

2.13.s:
deyamoṅkārapavane śrāddhamakṣayamicchatā /
śakrāvatāre gaṅgāyāṃ maināke ca nagottame //
2.13.d:
देयमोङ्कारपवने श्राद्धमक्षयमिच्छता ।
शक्रावतारे गङ्गायां मैनाके च नगोत्तमे ॥
2.13.m: śrāddha should be offered at Oṅkārapavana by one desiring inexhaustible fruit, / at Śakrāvatāra on the Gaṅgā, and on Maināka, the best of mountains;

2.13.s:
yamunāprabhave caiva sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate /
atyuṣṇāścātiśītāśca āpastasminnidarśanam //
2.13.d:
यमुनाप्रभवे चैव सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ।
अत्युष्णाश्चातिशीताश्च आपस्तस्मिन्निदर्शनम् ॥
2.13.m: and at the source of the Yamunā, one is freed from all sins. / The waters there are extremely hot and extremely cold—a visible proof;

2.13.s:
yamasya bhaginī puṣyā mārttaṇḍaduhitā śubhā /
tatrākṣayaṃ sadā śrāddhaṃ pitṛbhiḥ pūrvakīrttitam //
2.13.d:
यमस्य भगिनी पुष्या मार्त्तण्डदुहिता शुभा ।
तत्राक्षयं सदा श्राद्धं पितृभिः पूर्वकीर्त्तितम् ॥
2.13.m: she is the sister of Yama, the auspicious, bright daughter of the sun. / The ancestors formerly declared that a śrāddha offered there is ever inexhaustible.

2.13.s:
brahmatuṇḍahrade snātvā saddayo bhavati brāhmaṇaḥ /
tasmiṃstu śrāddhamānantyaṃ japahomatapāṃsi ca //
2.13.d:
ब्रह्मतुण्डह्रदे स्नात्वा सद्दयो भवति ब्राह्मणः ।
तस्मिंस्तु श्राद्धमानन्त्यं जपहोमतपांसि च ॥
2.13.m: Having bathed in the lake Brahmatuṇḍahrada, a brāhmaṇa instantly becomes pure; / and śrāddha, recitation, burnt offerings, and austerities performed there are unending.

2.13.s:
sthāṇubhūto 'carattatra vasiṣṭo vai mahātapāḥ /
adyāpi tatra dṛśyante pādapā maṇibarhaṇāḥ //
2.13.d:
स्थाणुभूतो ऽचरत्तत्र वसिष्टो वै महातपाः ।
अद्यापि तत्र दृश्यन्ते पादपा मणिबर्हणाः ॥
2.13.m: Vasiṣṭha of great asceticism wandered there, having become motionless as a tree trunk. / Even today, trees with jewels on their crests are seen there.

2.13.s:
tulā tu dṛśyate tatra dharmāndharmanidharśinī /
yathā vai tolitaṃ vipraistīrthānāṃ phalamuttamam //
2.13.d:
तुला तु दृश्यते तत्र धर्मान्धर्मनिधर्शिनी ।
यथा वै तोलितं विप्रैस्तीर्थानां फलमुत्तमम् ॥
2.13.m: A balance is seen there, demonstrating righteousness and unrighteousness, / just as the supreme fruit of sacred places was weighed by the brāhmaṇas.

2.13.s:
pitṝṇāṃ duhitā yogā gandhakālīti viśrutā /
caturtho brahmaṇastvaṃśaḥ parāśarakulodbhavaḥ //
2.13.d:
पितॄणां दुहिता योगा गन्धकालीति विश्रुता ।
चतुर्थो ब्रह्मणस्त्वंशः पराशरकुलोद्भवः ॥
2.13.m: The daughter of the ancestors, known through yoga as Gandhakālī, / [bore] the fourth part of Brahmā born in the family of Parāśara;

2.13.s:
vyasiṣyati caturddhā vai vedaṃ dhīmānmahāmuniḥ /
mahāyogaṃ mahātmānaṃ yā vyāsaṃ janayiṣyati //
2.13.d:
व्यसिष्यति चतुर्द्धा वै वेदं धीमान्महामुनिः ।
महायोगं महात्मानं या व्यासं जनयिष्यति ॥
2.13.m: the wise great sage divided the Veda fourfold— / she who gave birth to Vyāsa of great yoga and great soul.

2.13.s:
acchodakaṃ nāmasarastatrācchodāsamudbhavaḥ /
matsyayonau punarjātā niyogātkāraṇena tu //
2.13.d:
अच्छोदकं नामसरस्तत्राच्छोदासमुद्भवः ।
मत्स्ययोनौ पुनर्जाता नियोगात्कारणेन तु ॥
2.13.m: There was a lake named Acchodaka, where Acchodā arose; / she was born again in the womb of a fish by ordinance and for a reason.

2.13.s:
tasyāstvādyāśrame puṇye puṇyakṛdbhirniṣevite /
dattaṃ sakṛdapi śrāddhamakṣayaṃ samudāhṛtam //
2.13.d:
तस्यास्त्वाद्याश्रमे पुण्ये पुण्यकृद्भिर्निषेविते ।
दत्तं सकृदपि श्राद्धमक्षयं समुदाहृतम् ॥
2.13.m: At her original holy hermitage, frequented by performers of meritorious deeds, / a śrāddha offered even once is declared to be inexhaustible.

2.13.s:
nadyāṃ yogasamādhānaṃ dattaṃ yugapadudbhavet /
kuberatuṅge pāpaghnaṃ vyāsatīrthetathaiva ca //
2.13.d:
नद्यां योगसमाधानं दत्तं युगपदुद्भवेत् ।
कुबेरतुङ्गे पापघ्नं व्यासतीर्थेतथैव च ॥
2.13.m: Composure of mind [attained] through yoga at the river arises simultaneously with the offering; / and likewise, it destroys sins at Kuberatuṅga and at Vyāsatīrtha.

2.13.s:
puṇyāyāṃ brahmaṇo vedyāṃ śrāddhamānantyamiṣyate /
siddhaistu sevitā nityaṃ dṛśyate tu kṛtātmabhiḥ //
2.13.d:
पुण्यायां ब्रह्मणो वेद्यां श्राद्धमानन्त्यमिष्यते ।
सिद्धैस्तु सेविता नित्यं दृश्यते तु कृतात्मभिः ॥
2.13.m: Śrāddha offered on the holy altar of Brahmā is held to be unending; / always frequented by the Siddhas, it is seen by those whose minds are purified.

2.13.s:
anivartanaṃ tu nandāyāṃ vedyāḥ prāguttaradiśi /
siddhikṣetraṃ surairjuṣṭaṃ yatprāpya na nivarttate //
2.13.d:
अनिवर्तनं तु नन्दायां वेद्याः प्रागुत्तरदिशि ।
सिद्धिक्षेत्रं सुरैर्जुष्टं यत्प्राप्य न निवर्त्तते ॥
2.13.m: Anivartana is at the Nandā, in the north-eastern direction from the altar; / it is a field of perfection frequented by gods, reaching which one does not return.

2.13.s:
mahālaye padaṃ nyastaṃ mahādevena dhīmatā /
bhūtānāmanukaṃpārthaṃ nāstikānāṃ nidarśanam //
2.13.d:
महालये पदं न्यस्तं महादेवेन धीमता ।
भूतानामनुकंपार्थं नास्तिकानां निदर्शनम् ॥
2.13.m: At Mahālaya, a footprint was placed by wise Mahādeva, / for the sake of compassion toward beings and as a sign to unbelievers.

2.13.s:
viraje tvakṣayaṃ śrāddhaṃ pūrvameva mahālaye /
nandāyāṃ viraje caiva tathaiva ca mahālaye //
2.13.d:
विरजे त्वक्षयं श्राद्धं पूर्वमेव महालये ।
नन्दायां विरजे चैव तथैव च महालये ॥
2.13.m: A śrāddha at Viraja is indeed inexhaustible, previously [declared] at Mahālaya; / on the Nandā, and at Viraja, and likewise at Mahālaya,

2.13.s:
ātmānaṃ tārayantīha daśapūrvāndaśāparān /
kākahrade jātismaryaṃ suvarṇamamitaujasam //
2.13.d:
आत्मानं तारयन्तीह दशपूर्वान्दशापरान् ।
काकह्रदे जातिस्मर्यं सुवर्णममितौजसम् ॥
2.13.m: they save themselves, ten ancestors and ten descendants. / At Kākahrada there is memory of past births and gold of boundless splendor.

2.13.s:
kaumāraṃ ca saraḥ puṇyaṃ nāgabhogābhirakṣitam /
kumāratīrthe snātvā tu tridivaṃ yāti mānavaḥ //
2.13.d:
कौमारं च सरः पुण्यं नागभोगाभिरक्षितम् ।
कुमारतीर्थे स्नात्वा तु त्रिदिवं याति मानवः ॥
2.13.m: And the holy lake Kaumāra is protected by the coils of serpents; / having bathed at Kumāratīrtha, a man goes to heaven.

2.13.s:
devālaye tapastasvā ekapādena duścaram /
nirāhāro yugaṃ divyamumātuṅgo sthito jvalan //
2.13.d:
देवालये तपस्तस्वा एकपादेन दुश्चरम् ।
निराहारो युगं दिव्यमुमातुङ्गो स्थितो ज्वलन् ॥
2.13.m: Performing severe asceticism on one foot in the abode of the gods, / without food for a divine yuga, standing blazing at Umātuṅga,

2.13.s:
umātuṅge bhṛgostuṅge brahmatuṅge mahālaye /
tatra śrāddhāni deyāni nityamakṣayamicchatā //
2.13.d:
उमातुङ्गे भृगोस्तुङ्गे ब्रह्मतुङ्गे महालये ।
तत्र श्राद्धानि देयानि नित्यमक्षयमिच्छता ॥
2.13.m: at Umātuṅga, at Bhṛgutuṅga, at Brahmatuṅga, and at Mahālaya— / there śrāddhas should be offered constantly by one desiring inexhaustible fruit.

2.13.s:
akṣayaṃ tu sadā śrāddhaṃ śālagrāme samantataḥ /
duṣkṛtaṃ dṛśyate tatra pratyakṣamakṛtātmanām //
2.13.d:
अक्षयं तु सदा श्राद्धं शालग्रामे समन्ततः ।
दुष्कृतं दृश्यते तत्र प्रत्यक्षमकृतात्मनाम् ॥
2.13.m: A śrāddha is ever inexhaustible everywhere at Śālagrāma; / the evil deeds of the undisciplined are visibly seen there.

2.13.s:
pratyadeśo hyaśiṣṭānāṃ śiṣṭānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ /
tatra devahradaḥ puṇyo brahmaṇo nāgarāṭ śuciḥ //
2.13.d:
प्रत्यदेशो ह्यशिष्टानां शिष्टानां च विशेषतः ।
तत्र देवह्रदः पुण्यो ब्रह्मणो नागराट् शुचिः ॥
2.13.m: Indeed, it is a refutation of the undisciplined and especially [a test] of the disciplined. / There is the holy, pure Devahrada of Brahmā, the king of nāgas;

2.13.s:
piṇḍaṃ gṛhṇati hi satāṃ na gṛhṇātyasatāṃ sadā /
atipradīptairbhujagairbhoktumannaṃ na śakyate //
2.13.d:
पिण्डं गृह्णति हि सतां न गृह्णात्यसतां सदा ।
अतिप्रदीप्तैर्भुजगैर्भोक्तुमन्नं न शक्यते ॥
2.13.m: it takes the funeral ball of the virtuous, but never takes that of the unvirtuous. / The food cannot be consumed by the fiercely blazing serpents.

2.13.s:
pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyate dharmastīrthayornatayordvayoḥ /
kāravatyāṃ ca śāṇḍilyāṃ guhāyāṃ vāmanasya ca //
2.13.d:
प्रत्यक्षं दृश्यते धर्मस्तीर्थयोर्नतयोर्द्वयोः ।
कारवत्यां च शाण्डिल्यां गुहायां वामनस्य च ॥
2.13.m: Righteousness is visibly seen at the two bowed sacred places: / at the Kāravatī and at the Śāṇḍilī, and at the cave of Vāmana.

2.13.s:
gatvā caitāni pūtaḥsyācchradaddhamakṣayameva ca /
japo homastapo dhyānaṃ yatkiñcitsukṛtaṃ bhavet //
2.13.d:
गत्वा चैतानि पूतःस्याच्छ्रदद्धमक्षयमेव च ।
जपो होमस्तपो ध्यानं यत्किञ्चित्सुकृतं भवेत् ॥
2.13.m: Having gone to these, one becomes purified, and śrāddha is truly inexhaustible; / [as also are] recitation, burnt offerings, austerity, meditation, and whatever good deed there may be.

2.13.s:
brahmacaryaṃ ca yau dhatte gurubhaktiṃ śataṃ samāḥ /
evamādyāssaricchreṣṭhā yatsnānādaghamokṣaṇam /
kumāradhārā tatraiva dṛṣṭā pāpaṃ praṇaśyati //
2.13.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यं च यौ धत्ते गुरुभक्तिं शतं समाः ।
एवमाद्यास्सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा यत्स्नानादघमोक्षणम् ।
कुमारधारा तत्रैव दृष्टा पापं प्रणश्यति ॥
2.13.m: And whoever maintains celibacy and devotion to the guru for a hundred years— / such are the foremost rivers, by bathing in which release from sin [is attained]; / and there, merely on seeing Kumāradhārā, sin is destroyed.

2.13.s:
dhyānāsanaṃ tu tatraiva vyāsasyādyāpi dṛśyate /
śailaḥ kāntipurābhyāśe prāgudīcyāṃ diśi sthitaḥ //
2.13.d:
ध्यानासनं तु तत्रैव व्यासस्याद्यापि दृश्यते ।
शैलः कान्तिपुराभ्याशे प्रागुदीच्यां दिशि स्थितः ॥
2.13.m: Even today, the meditation seat of Vyāsa is seen right there, / on a mountain near Kāntipura, situated in the north-eastern direction.

2.13.s:
puṇya puṣkariṇī tatra kirātagaṇarakṣitā /
yasyāṃ snātvā sakṛdvipraḥ kāmānāpnoti śāśvatān //
2.13.d:
पुण्य पुष्करिणी तत्र किरातगणरक्षिता ।
यस्यां स्नात्वा सकृद्विप्रः कामानाप्नोति शाश्वतान् ॥
2.13.m: There is a holy lotus pond there, guarded by troops of Kirātas, / bathing in which once, a brāhmaṇa attains eternal desires;

2.13.s: adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ devavaccarate mahīm //
2.13.d: अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां देववच्चरते महीम् ॥
2.13.m: invisible to all beings, he wanders the earth like a god.

2.13.s:
kāśyapasya mahātīrthaṃ kālasarpiriti śrutam /
tatra śrāddhāni deyāni nityamakṣayamicchatā //
2.13.d:
काश्यपस्य महातीर्थं कालसर्पिरिति श्रुतम् ।
तत्र श्राद्धानि देयानि नित्यमक्षयमिच्छता ॥
2.13.m: The great sacred place of Kaśyapa is known as Kālasarpi; / there śrāddhas should be offered constantly by one desiring inexhaustible fruit.

2.13.s:
devadāruvane vāpi dhārāyāstu nidarśanam /
nirdhūtāni tu pāpāni dṛśyante sukṛtātmanām //
2.13.d:
देवदारुवने वापि धारायास्तु निदर्शनम् ।
निर्धूतानि तु पापानि दृश्यन्ते सुकृतात्मनाम् ॥
2.13.m: Or in the Devadāruvana, where there is the manifestation of the waterfall, / the cleansed sins of those of good deeds are visibly seen.

2.13.s:
bhāgīrathyāṃ prayāge tu nityamakṣayamucyate /
kālañjare daśārṇāyāṃ naimiṣe kurujāṅgale //
2.13.d:
भागीरथ्यां प्रयागे तु नित्यमक्षयमुच्यते ।
कालञ्जरे दशार्णायां नैमिषे कुरुजाङ्गले ॥
2.13.m: On the Bhāgīrathī at Prayāga, [a śrāddha] is said to be constantly inexhaustible; / at Kālañjara, on the Daśārṇā, in Naimiṣa, in Kurujāṅgala,

2.13.s:
vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ ca deyaṃ śrāddhaṃ prayatnataḥ /
tatra yogeśvaro nityaṃ tasyāṃ dattamathākṣayam //
2.13.d:
वाराणस्यां नगर्यां च देयं श्राद्धं प्रयत्नतः ।
तत्र योगेश्वरो नित्यं तस्यां दत्तमथाक्षयम् ॥
